Here God speaks when his act of producing is understood, just as the Lord himself said to holy Job: “Or do you think that I spoke to you in any other way than so that you might appear righteous?” He said that he had spoken through that tribulation by which he caused Job to be tested.

“Nothing on earth happens without cause, and pain does not arise from the ground” (Job 5:6).

“From the ground”—that is, from the whole nature of the earth—evil will not arise, since nothing on earth occurs without God’s justice. This is said to mean that no natural evil exists; this is what he calls “pain,” whereas every evil that occurs is accidental to good nature.

There is another evil, namely that of punishment, which God inflicts upon human beings because of sin. Sin is indeed evil, but through free choice it is evil—something committed by human will. There is also the repayment of evil, that is, of sin, when the Lord inflicts punishments upon sinners. The point, therefore, is that none of these accidental evils occurs without God’s judgment. It is not natural to man in such a way that it should be thought to have been created by God; therefore it is said: “And pain does not arise from the ground”—that is, it arises not from nature but from guilt.

“Man is born to labor, and the bird to flight” (Job 5:7).

That is, labor awaits [or perhaps: admonishes] man, so that, chastened by all vices, he may proceed. He becomes so awake and alert for this purpose that, like a bird which naturally takes to flight, he too may fly upward through the struggles of the present life toward the things above.

“Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night in which it was said, ‘A man has been conceived’” (Job 3:2).

Jeremiah also says: “Cursed be the day on which I was born.”

Some say that the times of human birth, having passed, cannot be cursed. Certainly they are cursed to no purpose, since they have already run their course. These holy men, filled with the spirit of prophecy, curse the day of human birth; yet they do so not without their own suffering. For, by compassion with the human race, they perceive within themselves God’s sentence of death imposed upon it. I therefore do not think that the day given to man for his service is cursed by the saints with such an execration.

Let us understand, then, that “day,” together with its “night,” is spoken tropically (*tropikōs*, τροπικῶς). Day and night may be understood as the Devil and mortality—not because the Devil is day and light, but because he was once a day, when he dwelt with God, the eternal light, just as Lucifer is from the dawn of morning and as a stone shines with radiance in the paradise of God. Alternatively, it may be because the day seems to exist for the impious and sinners who rejoice in the prosperity and happiness of this age. Of them it is said: “His light shall be taken away from the wicked.” And Solomon says: “The light of the wicked shall be extinguished.” Again: “The splendor of the wicked is sin.” This too can be said of the Devil, who is the inventor of sin.

“And he formed man.” You see, therefore, how great the difference is between making and forming. What God made in his image, namely the soul, he made; what he formed is the body from earth, which he vivified by the inspiration of the soul. The image pertains to immortality; the likeness of God to power and activity, so that nature might possess the image of God’s immortality and the likeness of his power over all that he had created, and might imitate God through righteous works.

“God speaks once, and does not repeat the same thing a second time.”

From the very beginning of the world and thereafter, God has always spoken to human beings, and nevertheless he speaks once. But when the Lord is said to speak frequently, either his law is manifold or the diversity of his prophets and commandments is indicated. When he is said to speak once, however, his settled and determined judgment is demonstrated.

For “God’s speaking” is understood as his act of producing. Thus the Lord himself says to holy Job: “Or do you think that I spoke to you in any other way than so that you might appear righteous?” He says that he spoke through the tribulation by which he caused Job to be tested. Therefore, for him, speaking is the same as doing.

Elihu says accordingly: “God speaks once, and does not repeat the same thing a second time.” He is said to speak again—that is, to make a change—only if this very change in our life should demand it.

“All human beings see him; each person beholds him from afar.”

Through the good of their nature, knowledge of the Creator is present in human hearts. Even if someone is so depraved and cold that he strives to be alienated from his Creator, there is no one who can hide from his warmth. Therefore every mortal, although from afar, senses and understands God.

This perception is wholly unlike that by which a body created by the Spirit perceives the Lord to exist. Rather, it occurs in another ineffable manner, by which God is to be viewed with the mind’s eye. In the very gaze of the heart, through understanding, a person sees that God is above him.

If you carefully compare this with the Commentary which we have specifically said should be attributed to Philip, you will perceive that the chief difference is almost entirely what the ingenuity of an attentive epitomizer introduced. Although the various interpretations we have so far reviewed were copied from that one work, you must nevertheless admit that his Commentary itself was not entirely free from additions by another compiler or from abridgements, nor preserved in complete and native authenticity.

# Interlinear Exposition of the Book of Job

[Note: In Migne, in each chapter, the Exposition is printed between the lines of the biblical text.]

## Chapter One
[Col. 1408] a There was a man in the land of Uz, named c Job; and [Col. 1409A] that man was d simple and upright, fearing God and turning away from evil. And seven sons and three daughters were born to him. His possessions were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, together with a very large household; and that man was greater than all the people of the East. His sons used to go and hold banquets in their houses, each on his appointed day. And they sent for their three sisters, inviting them to eat and drink with them. When the days of the banquet had gone around, Job sent for them and sanctified them; rising early, he offered holocausts for each one. For Job said: “Perhaps my sons have sinned and blessed God in their hearts.” Thus Job did every day.

Now on a certain day, when [Col. 1409C] the angels [Vulgate: sons] of God had come to stand before the Lord, Satan also was present among them. The Lord said to him: “Where have you come from?” He answered: “I have gone around the earth and traveled through it.” And the Lord said to him: “Have you considered my child Job, that there is none like him on earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil?” Satan answered him: “Does Job fear God for nothing? Have you not [Col. 1409D] fenced him in, his house and all his possessions on every side, and blessed the works of his hands, so that his possessions have increased in the land? But stretch out your hand a little, and touch everything he possesses; surely he will bless you to your face.” Then the Lord said to Satan: “Behold, everything he has is in your hand; only do not [Col. 1410A] stretch out your hand against him.” And Satan went out from the presence of the Lord.

When one day his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother, a messenger came to Job and said: “The oxen were plowing, and the she-asses were grazing beside them; then the Sabeans fell upon them and took everything, and struck the servants with the sword. I alone escaped to tell you.” While he was still speaking, another came and said: “The fire of God fell from heaven and consumed the sheep and the servants that it touched; I alone escaped [Col. 1410B] to tell you.” While he was still speaking, another came and said: “The Chaldaeans formed three bands, attacked the camels, and took them; they also struck the servants with the sword, and I alone escaped to tell you.” He was still speaking when another entered and said: “While your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother, suddenly a violent wind [Col. 1410C] swept in from the region of the desert and consumed [Vulgate: shook] the four corners of the house. When it collapsed, it crushed your children, and they died; I alone escaped to tell you.”

Then Job rose, tore his garment, and, with his head shorn, fell to the ground and worshiped. He said: “Naked I came forth from my mother’s womb, and naked I shall return there. The Lord [Col. 1410D] gave, the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord forever” [this is absent from the Vulgate]. In all this Job did not sin, nor did he speak anything foolish against God.

[Col. 1407] a “Man” is said from the strength of his spirit, by which he overcame temptations.

b Cush and Bus were sons of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. The land of Cush signifies the man assumed from Mary [Col. 1408]. It is interpreted as “counselor.”

c Job is interpreted as “suffering.” He bore the type of Christ.

[Col. 1409A] d As the Apostle says: “I want you to be wise in what is good, but simple in what is evil.” He possessed these four virtues. To fear God means to omit none of the good things that ought to be done: the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, the Law, Prophecy, and the Gospel. The perfect number signifies the perfect life of the Church and signifies Christ’s people. The Gentile people. The people of Jews and Gentiles are signified, as by clean and unclean animals. The house signifies the Church multiplied in faith through diverse graces. He was richer than all who lived in the East. The father is also called rich, and the sons harmonious: the father’s substance was to be divided among them, yet an undivided charity preserved the hearts of all.

[Col. 1409B] The seven days were completed. By this also he displayed his holiness and piety, because he desired to present them to God blameless, just as he desired to present himself. Here it appears that he was the firstborn, since he offered holocausts and sacrifice. The writer changed the sense. Secure because of his works, he therefore cleansed their hearts.

[Col. 1409C] Let us understand not only the angels of God but also all the saints. He was permitted to insert himself among the just. This does not express ignorance on God’s part; rather, without knowing the devil’s ways of pride, he condemned them. Through this the devil’s labor, and how great it was, is discerned. He scorned standing in heaven, [lacuna] justifying his elect, [lacuna] surely he would have been an apostate angel. The same as above. It is as though he said openly: “When one receives so many good things on earth, what wonder is it if he conducts himself innocently on their account?”

[Col. 1409D] It is as though he said: “Take away what you have given; for if he loses what he has received, he will not seek the regard of your grace once temporal possessions have been removed.” This was said by antiphrasis, because the historian’s writer did not dare, in his own words, to speak a blasphemous word against God. Great is the piety of our Lord: he permits and restrains our enemy, loosens and curbs him. He exposes the substance, yet protects the body, which he will later hand over to the tempter; nevertheless, he does not release the enemy against everything at once, lest, striking from every side, he break the citizen.

[Col. 1410A] He went out from his presence because, having received the power of temptation, he attained the desires of his wickedness. The oxen were plowing so that, by recalling the fruit of their labor, the cause of grief might increase. The devil did all these things so that Job, exasperated by so many calamities, might burst forth into blasphemy against the Lord, concerning whom God had previously borne great testimony. It is as though he said: “You endure the punishment of him whom you wished to appease with so many sacrifices; you tolerate the anger of him whom you served daily with toil.”

[Col. 1410B] Behold, again, lest he should seem to have grieved too little over human adversity, he announces that the Chaldaean bands have attacked. The Sabeans and Chaldaeans are the devastators and persecutors of the Church, who strive through the perversity of heresy to scatter the Lord’s flocks and the house of Christ. The crafty enemy first announced small things, then greater ones; finally he brought about the death of the children, so as to break the holy man’s patience. They were feasting in the house of the elder brother when they perished, because when the greater devote themselves to pleasures, the reins of wantonness are plainly loosened in the lesser.

[Col. 1410C] It is known that the elements cannot be moved without a heavenly command. It is covertly implied that he himself moved the elements who permitted them to be moved. This signifies strength of endurance. It signifies mourning, not sadness arising from despair, and the separation of the pious from the impious. It signifies that superfluous and useless things must be cut away. The earth produces man naked and receives him naked. He was sprinkled with no stain of original sin. These words apply to Christ. He was destined to return to his own flesh through the resurrection.

[Col. 1410D] He took the good as his inheritance and took away the wicked. The one who gave took back what was his; he did not take away what was ours. For he neither swelled silently in his conscience nor loosened his tongue into insolence. He could not speak foolishly against the Father’s wisdom.

## CHAPTER II

Now it happened that on a certain day the sons of God came and stood before the Lord, and Satan also came among them and stood in his sight. The Lord said to [Col. 1411A] Satan: “Where have you come from?” He answered: “I have gone around the earth and traveled through it.” And the Lord said to Satan: “Have you considered my child [Vulgate: servant] Job, that there is none like him on earth, a blameless man, fearing God and turning away from evil, and still holding fast to his innocence?” Yet you have stirred me against him, so that I afflicted him without cause.” Satan answered him: “Skin [Col. 1411B] for skin, and everything that a man has he will give for his life. But stretch out your hand and touch his bone and his flesh, and then you will see whether he will bless you to your face.” Then the Lord said to Satan: “Behold, he is in your hand; nevertheless, preserve his life” [Vulgate: guard his soul]. Satan therefore went out from the presence of the Lord and struck Job with a most grievous ulcer, from the sole of his foot to his neck [Vulgate: crown of his head] [Col. 1411C]. He scraped the discharge with a potsherd, sitting on a dungheap.

His wife said to him: “Do you still persist in your simplicity? Bless God and die.” He answered her: “You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things from the hand of the Lord, why should we not receive evil?” In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

When Job’s three friends heard of all the evil that had happened to him, they came, each from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite [Alternative: Suchite], and Zophar the Naamathite [Vulgate: Naamathite]. They had agreed to come together to visit him and console him. When they lifted their eyes from afar, they did not recognize him; and crying aloud, they wept. They tore their garments and scattered dust over their heads toward heaven. They sat with him on the ground [Col. 1412A] for seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great. After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day, and he spoke.

[Col. 1410D] The spirits of the angels return there by conversion from which they do not depart through any turning away of mind. Although he lost blessedness, he did not lose a nature like theirs; and, as Scripture says, the eyes of the Lord observe [Col. 1411A] the good and the wicked. This is not because of ignorance, but so that it might be shown to us what the enemy answered the Lord. Because, while they do not desire inward things, they are wearied by labor in outward things. “Adversary” is the interpretation. We have explained these matters above, piece by piece; we avoid repeating what we have said.

It is not as though the Lord had been incited by the devil to tempt Job, but rather as if he were saying: “What benefit did you gain by refusing to believe that Job was a most steadfast man in adversity?” It is as though he were mocking Job, saying that, to save his life, he would give the devil his possessions for destruction. As though the evil he had inflicted on blessed Job were not enough, he asks that his flesh also be struck.

[Col. 1411B] Behold, he is again permitted to be tempted, but protection accompanies him so that he may not fall. He is said to “observe,” that is, he is not permitted to break in. He was prohibited from part of the temptation. We explained above how Satan goes out from the presence of the Lord. Some believe this was the disease of elephantiasis, and therefore that he abandoned his kingdom because of excessive foulness. Considering himself clay and fragile, [Col. 1411C] he showed his body quickly becoming foul. The devil incited the woman’s tongue, but by this strategy he achieved nothing. By these words she taught him to abandon his simplicity. The same meaning as above. Therefore those who blaspheme the Lord must be counted among fools.

Great consolation in tribulation comes when, while suffering adversities, we recall the gifts of our creator. He gave thanks to the Father who scourged him and supplied instruction to the wife who offered wicked counsel. The three kings were of the race of Esau. [Col. 1411D] Teman was the province in which he ruled. Those who came by agreement to console the afflicted demonstrated the extent of their charity; yet they sinned through heedless speech. Still, they could easily merit pardon because they sought him with good intention. He represents heretics who believe in God while rejecting the man, and thus tear apart the faith of the Church. They cover their hearts with an earthly and mortal understanding. In these matters the whole span of the heretics’ life is displayed: they sat always, seven days and nights, with afflicted Job, whether they persisted in confessing the faith. Whether they adhered to him with such constant and repeated visitation through exactly that many days and nights, we do not know. This is what the historian-writer says, whom tradition holds to have been Moses.

## CHAPTER III

May the day perish on which I was born, and the night in which it was said: “A man has been conceived.” May that day [Col. 1412B] be turned into darkness; may God not seek it from above, and may it not be illumined by light. May darkness and the shadow of death obscure it; may gloom seize it, and may it be wrapped in bitterness. May a dark whirlwind possess that night; may it not be counted among the days of the year or numbered among the months. May that night be solitary and unworthy of praise. May those who curse the day curse it, those who are ready to awaken [Col. 1412C] Leviathan. May its stars be darkened by gloom; may it wait and not see, nor behold the rising of the dawn. For it did not close the doors of the womb that carried me, nor remove evil from my eyes.

Why did I not die in the womb, or perish immediately upon coming forth from the uterus? Why was I received upon knees? Why was I suckled [Col. 1412D] at the breasts? For now I would sleep and be silent, and I would rest in my sleep, with the kings and rulers of the earth who build solitudes for themselves, or with princes who possess gold and fill their houses with silver; or, like a hidden miscarriage, I would not exist, like those conceived who never saw the light.

There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there those weary in strength rest. And [Col. 1413A] formerly the prisoners rest together without distress. They do not hear the voice of the taskmaster. Small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.

Why is light given to the wretched, and life to those who are in bitterness of soul? To those who await death and it does not come, who rejoice exceedingly as though digging for treasure when they have found a tomb; to the man whose [Vulgate: for whom] [Col. 1413B] life is hidden, and whom God has surrounded with darkness?

Before I eat, I sigh; and my roaring is like overflowing waters. For the fear that I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me. Have I not dissembled? Have I not been silent? Have I not rested? Yet indignation has come upon me.

[Col. 1412A] The patient man does not speak from anger, but desires that immortality, destroyed through Adam, return through Christ. He understands the day together with the night as spoken of. It signifies the devil and death.

[Col. 1412B] May its memory not be before the Lord for good. The light of knowledge of God, or of repentance. May it be blinded by the multitude of sins. Infernal punishment. Blindness of the heart. The fury of God’s anger, of which it was said above. The devil, who brought disturbance into the world. Within the number of Christians, because the year signifies Christ in the Apostles. May it not have God as its inhabitant.

The saints certainly curse the transgression of their death and the devil by resisting his dominion—that is, the addition of men who do not cease increasing men’s guilt. Sinners who, in the night of the world, thought themselves to shine in honor and riches. May the devil not recognize the light of Christ’s redemptions. The resurrection of Christ. He ought to have been held in his mother’s womb as in strong prison-bars, lest he be born into sorrows: continual pains and torments.

[Col. 1412C] Why did mortality itself not destroy the mortal? Why should I live, destined to die and to suffer the evils of human mortality? After the manifest fault, why did habit still receive me into it? After the habit of guilt, why was I nourished for its increase? So that I would produce no weeping or howling.

[Col. 1412D] I was not driven on by the goads of torments. Although they are in hell, their bodies nevertheless do not feel the torments. Vain works, or because all things are deserted that do not have Christ as a guest. He says this because of the abundance of riches. In various ways he says that he wished to escape the punishments in which he was. Those miscarried are men before the written Law. Those who were born into this world after receiving the Law and did not see the coming of Christ.

Because the glory of the proud will be humbled in hell, liberated from the oppression and trouble of the world. In [Col. 1413A] hell, he says, they dwell together, yet without punishment. They do not fear the commands of wicked masters. The small and great among believers are there freed from shame. Since, as I see, there is equality of persons in hell, why has life, full of torments, been given to me, wretched man? Because of their anguish, people seek death; they rejoice exceedingly when they find the burial they desired.

He easily finds treasure who drives away from himself the burden of earthly thought. He who desires to mortify himself rejoices greatly when he finds the rest of contemplation. He speaks of himself, because the merit of his life was hidden [Col. 1413B]. The torments of punishments. Among the other torments, the devil had also inflicted this sickness on him: that he should be tormented before food, and after food suffer unceasing pains; he added what follows concerning this. It is as though he said: “I feared offending God by sinning; what benefit did it bring me, since he torments me with pains?” Not returning evil, he indicates silence from idle words. He speaks of the mass of his wounds.

## CHAPTER IV

Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: If we begin to speak to you, perhaps you will take it badly; but who can restrain the word conceived in the mind? Behold, you have instructed many and strengthened weary hands. Your words have supported those who were wavering, and you have strengthened the knees of those who trembled. But now the scourge has come upon you, and you have failed; it has touched you, and you are troubled. Where is your fear, your strength, your patience, and the perfection of your ways?

Remember, I beg you: when did the innocent ever perish? Or when were the upright [Col. 1413D] destroyed? Rather, I have seen those who work iniquity and sow sorrows reap them; they perish when God breathes, and are consumed by the breath of his anger. The roar of the lion, the voice of the lioness, and the teeth of the lion’s whelps are broken. The tiger perishes because it has no prey, and the lion’s cubs are scattered.

Now a hidden word was spoken to me, and my ear received, as if furtively, the veins of its whisper. In the horror of a nighttime vision, when sleep usually overwhelms human beings, fear and trembling seized me, and all my bones were terrified. When a spirit passed before me, with me present, the hairs of my flesh bristled. Someone stood there whose face I did not recognize; an image was before my eyes, and I heard a voice like a gentle breeze.

Can a man be justified in comparison with God, or can a man be purer than his maker? Behold, those who serve him are not steadfast, and he found perversity in his angels; how much more in those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is earthly? They will be consumed like a moth. From morning to evening they will be cut down, and because no one understands, they will perish forever. Those who remain [Col. 1414C] will be taken away from them; they will die, and not in wisdom.

[Col. 1413B] He shows that he is going to speak not consoling but injurious words; therefore, through words conceived, he inflicts an insult upon the hearer. You recalled many from error. By your goodness you consoled the poor. You strengthened those who were uncertain about their religion. All these things are said against holy Job with mockery, as they turn away from uprightness. He did not fail or become troubled, but blessed the Lord in everything. It is as though he said: “If you had possessed fear of God and perfection of life, you would never have suffered such things.”

Thus he speaks in ignorance of Abel, who was innocent when killed, and of the just who were frequently afflicted. [Col. 1413D] We know that those who work iniquity perish while anger rages, just as we have seen happen to you. He repeats what he had said earlier. He displays the savagery of the one who seizes prey, in which he falsely marks holy Job. He calls the cubs more rapacious toward prey, that is, he says that Job’s sons were like him. He shows their speed in seizing prey and plundering people. Their sons were likewise killed.

A divine secret shown to me by revelation, that is, the cause of your punishments. The force of the sentence secretly reached the ears of my heart. Here he asserts that he did not see some empty fantasy of a dream, but a true vision. To make the account of the dream more credible, he specifies the time. He says that he was exceedingly terrified by the unusual vision. He wishes to show an angel, as Daniel says of himself: “In the vision my frame was loosened.” An unknown face produced greater fear. He says that he saw by a hidden faith one whom he had not previously known, and that the figure gently said to him what follows.

[Col. 1414B] A creature cannot be compared with the creator, because human justice, compared with divine justice, is injustice. He speaks of the devil and of those who fell from their nature into vice. It is understood of human nature, because from our very dwellings we are shown to be base. Just as garments are consumed by a moth, so bodies are consumed by death. “Morning” signifies the whole life of human beings, which fails in old age. He says this concerning unbelievers. He understands it of believers. The saints are separated from the impious. Fools are those who do not possess the wisdom of the fear of God.

## CHAPTER V

Call, then, if there is anyone who will answer you, and turn to some one of the saints. Anger kills the foolish man, and envy kills the little one. I have seen the fool firmly rooted, and suddenly I cursed his beauty. His sons will be far from salvation; they will be crushed at the gate, and there will be no one to rescue them. The hungry will eat his harvest, and the armed man will seize him; the thirsty will drink his wealth.

Nothing occurs on earth without cause, and sorrow does not spring from the ground. Man is born for labor, and the bird for flight. Therefore I will entreat the Lord and place my speech before God, who does great and unsearchable things, and wonders without number; who gives rain upon the face of the earth and waters everything; who sets the lowly on high and raises the sorrowful to safety; who scatters the thoughts of the wicked, so that they cannot accomplish with their hands what they have begun; who catches the wise in their craftiness and scatters the counsel of the perverse.

By day they will encounter darkness and, as at night, grope about at midday. But he will save the poor man from the sword of their mouth and from the hand of the violent. The needy will have hope, but iniquity will close its mouth.

Blessed is the man who is corrected by God. Therefore do not reject the chastening of the Lord, because he wounds and heals; he strikes, and his hands will heal. In six tribulations he will deliver you, and in the seventh evil will not touch you. In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war from the hand of the sword. You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and you will not fear calamity when it comes. In devastation and famine you will laugh, and you will not fear the beasts of the earth. But you will have a covenant with the stones of the region, and the beasts will be at peace with you. You will know that your tent is at peace, and, visiting your dwelling, you will not sin.

You will also know that your seed will be numerous and your offspring like the grass of the earth. You will enter the grave in abundance, as a heap is brought in at its proper time. Behold, this is how it is, as we have investigated it; having heard it, consider it in your mind.

[Col. 1414C] Up to this point he speaks of the things he says he saw in dreams; thereafter he rebukes holy Job. “Of men or angels, if any of them answers you otherwise.” He calls him angry because he cursed his day. He marks him as fainthearted and envious. One who thinks himself fixed forever. He calls the beauty of passing prosperity. All these things, as I have said several times, are spoken as a reproach against holy Job; they will be condemned by the public judgment of all.

The devil devours the labor of the sinful man, being called armed and hungry in his betrayal of human beings. Evil men who seize the resources of others. When slowness benefits the diligent by delaying the reward, and speed increases the punishment of the lazy. Without justice. Human nature was good, but evil occurred. As a bird flies by nature, so man ascends to higher things through labor.

Granting me nothing on account of justice or merit, I will say this before him, which commends my humility to him. The operation of all things is unsearchable to human beings.

[Col. 1415A] As it is said: “He makes his rain fall upon the just and the unjust” (Matthew 5:45); he displays the abundance of doctrine. The saints in the kingdom, as it is said: “Blessed are those who mourn now” (ibid., 5), and so forth. The persecutors of Christ’s martyrs, so that they cannot accomplish what they desire; or the hands of those persecutors against the Church of God. It signifies the craftiness of worldly people. Through the voice of the Gospel, he counts it as foolishness. The Jews fell from the day of the Law into the darkness of faithlessness, and thus found tribulation, just as previously they had prosperity. Christ, who became poor for us, was delivered from the blasphemies of the Jews.

[Col. 1415B] The hope of the resurrection belongs to Christ; the blasphemy of the Jews is rightly stopped. As it is said: “Whom the Lord loves, he chastises.” These things are rightly said against holy Job as against a transgressor, who is instructed by the Lord as a son. As it is said: “I kill and I make alive.” Immediately afterward he enumerates the six themselves: hearing the word of God; sin, from the power of death; from [Col. 1415C] the unbridled tongue, vengeance upon evils. You will rejoice when you see others destroyed by devastation. The power of the devil, or of earthly men. You will always have peace with all the saints. Good men changed from bestial life. Your body will be freed from all punishments. Presenting yourself as worthy of divine visitation. Carnal sons, or the fruits of good works. Because of their multitude they are compared with grass.

[Col. 1415D] You will die full of days, or in an abundance of good works. Just as wheat goes into the granaries, so the saints enter into glory. That is, what you yourself ought to receive in your heart for your correction.

## CHAPTER VI

Job answered and said: Would that my sins, by which I deserved wrath, and the calamity that I suffer were weighed in a balance; it would appear heavier than the sand of the sea. [Col. 1416A] Therefore my words are full of pain, because the arrows of the Lord are in me; their indignation drinks up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord wage war against me.

Does the wild ass bray when it has grass, or does the ox low when there is a full manger before it? Or can what is tasteless and unsalted be eaten? Can anyone taste what, once tasted, brings death? [Col. 1416B] What my soul previously refused to touch is now, because of anguish, my food. Who will grant that my petition may come, and that God may give me what I desire? May he who began it himself crush me, release his hand, and cut me off; and may this be my consolation: that, afflicting me with pain, he not spare me, and that I not contradict the words of the Holy One.

What is my strength that I should endure? Or what is my end, that I should act patiently? [Col. 1416C] My strength is not the strength of stones, nor is my flesh bronze. Behold, there is no help for me in myself, and even those close to me have withdrawn from me. Whoever removes mercy from his friend has abandoned the fear of the Lord.

My brothers have passed me by like a torrent that quickly rushes through the valleys. Those who fear the frost will be overtaken by snow; when they are scattered [Col. 1416D] they will perish, and when they grow warm they will dissolve from their place. Their paths of walking are entangled; they will wander in vain and perish.

Consider Tema and the roads of Sheba. Wait a little, and see: they are confounded because I hoped. They have also come as far as me, and they are covered with shame. Now you have come, and, merely seeing my wound, you are afraid.

Have I said: “Bring me something, and give me a gift from your substance”? Or: “Deliver me from the hand of the enemy, and rescue me from the hand of the mighty”? [Col. 1417A] Teach me, and I will be silent; and if perhaps I have been ignorant of something, instruct me. Why have you detracted from the words of truth, when there is no one among you who can convict me? You compose speeches merely for rebuke and utter words into the wind. You rush upon an orphan and strive to overthrow your friend.

Nevertheless, complete what you have begun. [Col. 1417B] Give ear and see whether I am lying. Answer, I beg you, without contention; speak what you judge to be just, and you will find no iniquity in my mouth, nor will folly resound in my throat.

[Col. 1415D] Since you say that I suffer these things because of my sins, I would have my sins weighed against the calamity I suffer, and you would immediately see them to be light; the calamity itself is heavier than the merit of my sins.

[Col. 1416A] For, as I said, the punishments are greater than the deserts of my offenses. The distress of punishments is compared with arrows; these signify not only punishments but also the worms which the devil stirred up to suck his blood. To increase the punishments, the devil instills terror in him. These animals, if they have abundant fodder, utter no sound of complaint. But he is hemmed in by anguish, so that he speaks harshly.

I have done nothing without faith; how do I suffer what I endure? He has spoken no foolish word against God, nothing lacking faith. Just as everyone recoils from something deadly, so I feared touching sin.

[Col. 1416B] Now I feed on bitter words, which previously I feared to bring forth from my mouth. He desired and longed to be freed from torments through death. Just as I suffer punishments with God’s permission, so may death crush me by his power. May this be my consolation: that I obtain an end to my torments through the remedy of death. This is appropriate to the humility of the saints.

“I am a little human being; how can I endure such scourges?” It is as though he said: “If I knew the end of my pain, I would await it patiently.” I am not insensitive to pain like stones, because my flesh is corrupted by discharge. Sorrow refuses to allow my soul to be consoled. The Prophet says the same concerning Christ: “My friends and my neighbors” (Isaiah 37:12), and what follows.

Whoever does not sympathize from the heart with the afflicted abandons the commandments of God. All his kin detested him and, abandoning him swiftly, lamented those who had fallen to the depths like a torrent. I feared committing even small sins, and now I am tormented as though I had committed great ones.

[Col. 1416C] In these verses he recalls the day of his affliction. Just as snow melts in the heat of the sun, so his glory did not appear. The strength of his spirit was wrapped in punishments. Those who are destined to perish labor in vain. A province. The province from which people flocked to him.

[Col. 1417A] Since they cannot bend me toward despair by their foolish rebukes, they themselves are confounded. Seeing his pain, they covered their faces in shame. His friends feared a similar collapse of wounds for themselves.

It is as though he said: “Did I ask anything of you, or am I unworthy of your strength, that you mock me as though I were needy and poor?” Rebuke me if I am lying; I will be silent when convicted, and if there is something else I do not know, it is your duty to correct me who am in error.

Although only Eliphaz had spoken, the minds of the others held the same view; therefore he spoke of them all in the plural. The speech of the foregoing speaker is filled with exceedingly biting rebukes. They spoke vainly of their own will. He was deserted like an orphan by all his own. Through mockery and derision. Through the words of Eliphaz. Understand in your heart that I am not lying. Let there be no eagerness to contradict, which generates the disease of contention; then, undisturbed by any darkness of hostility, you will be able to judge what is just between me and you.

## CHAPTER VII

The life of man upon earth is a warfare, and his days are like the days of a hired laborer. As a servant longs for shade, and as a hired laborer awaits the end of his work, so I have had empty months and counted laborious nights for myself. If I sleep, when shall I rise? And again I shall await the evening, and be filled with pains until darkness.

My flesh is clothed with rottenness and the filth of dust. My skin has dried out and contracted. My days have passed more quickly than a web is cut by the weaver; they have been consumed without any hope.

Remember that my life is a wind, and [Col. 1417D] my eye will not return to see good things; nor will the sight of man look upon me. Your eyes are upon me, and I shall not remain. As a cloud is consumed and passes away, so one who descends to the underworld will not ascend, nor will he return again to his house; his place will no longer know him.

Therefore I will not spare my mouth; I will speak in the tribulation of my spirit. I will converse in the bitterness [Col. 1418A] of my soul. Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you have surrounded me with a prison? If I say, “My bed will comfort me, and I will be relieved when I speak with myself on my couch,” you will terrify me through dreams and shake me with horror through visions.

Therefore my soul has chosen hanging, and my bones death. I have despaired; I shall no longer live. Spare me, for my days are nothing. What is man, that you magnify him, or why do you set your heart upon him? You visit him at dawn and suddenly test him.

How long will you not spare me, nor grant me [Vulgate: me] time to swallow my saliva? I have sinned; what shall I do to you, O guardian of men? Why have you set me against you, and have I become a burden to myself? Why do you not take away my sin, and why do you not remove my iniquity? Behold, now I shall sleep in the dust, and if you seek me in the morning, I shall not remain.

[Col. 1417B] Men of God fighting against vices. Just as servants and hired laborers desire the wage of their servitude and labor, so those laboring for God await eternal rewards. (On recompense in the age.) In these words he indicates the persistence of his sufferings, and that, for relief from his sufferings, he desired a change of circumstances, seeking day in the night and night in the day. He was struck by this wound by the devil from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head—that is, he was wholly corrupted. He compared the frailty of the flesh to threads of a web. I have not placed confidence of mind in the present life. He is like a passing wind, because now my spirit has already passed away through grief, [and so has] the perception of my mind. When [Col. 1417D] he said these things, he did not know that he would return to glory. A human being will not look upon me in that glory in which I formerly was. I cannot endure the anger of your vision. Man will be restored from the dust of the earth in the likeness of a cloud. He does not ascend into incorruption, but is clothed with immortality. The spirit into its own body. The former manner of life of the world in the changed human being. I shall say what enormity of punishments has produced for me, and I shall speak with bitterness, because of the anguish [Col. 1418A] of the punishments. As though he were saying: The sea and the sea-monster—the wicked and impious, and their leader, the evil spirit, rightly a sea creature—are confined in prison, not I. He calls every pain of punishment a prison. If amid sufferings I turn myself toward rest, I shall be relieved by the comfort of my bed, if there too I should wish to speak with myself in order to relieve my pains. He said that he suffered this from the Lord, because the devil was permitted by the Lord to inflict those things upon him. As though he were saying: It is better for me, under the affliction of punishments, to think about my death than to inflict blasphemy upon your majesty. Because I said what I ought not to have said, [Col. 1418B] or because I abandoned the goods of the present life for the sake of the speech I uttered. Be gracious to one who beseeches you, lest I be found being punished there, where the days are without end. He humbly confesses God’s compassion toward him. That you should apply solicitous care to him? After the darkness of ignorance, you illuminate him with divine knowledge, you who know human hearts. From these punishments which I suffer by your permission—for this was among the other evils of his sufferings: speaking what he ought not to have spoken. What correction, then, can I offer you, who are just? You who know all things. Why did you give me the opportunity to answer, as I said? A just man ought not to suffer such things, who answered you [Col. 1418C] with what he ought not to have said, because a creature ought not to speak against the Creator. The pains through which I am compelled to sin, although until now I had been just. As though he were lamenting and saying: In the present life I indeed suffer the death of the flesh, and yet I fear an even heavier sentence. At the morning of the resurrection.

## CHAPTER VIII

Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: How long will you speak such things, and [how long will] the spirit of the many words [Col. 1418D] of your mouth [continue]? Does God pervert judgment, or does the Almighty subvert what is just? Even if your sons sinned against him, he dismissed them into the hand of their iniquity. Yet if you rise at dawn to God and supplicate the Almighty; if you walk pure and upright, he will immediately awaken for you and restore the habitation of your righteousness in peace. So much so that, if your former circumstances were small, your latter ones will be greatly increased [Col. 1419A]. For ask the former generation and diligently investigate the memory of the fathers. For we are of yesterday and do not know, because our days upon the earth are like a shadow. They themselves will teach you; they will speak to you and bring forth words from their heart. Can the rush live without moisture, or can the reed grow [Vulg. “the papyrus grow”] without water? While it is still in flower and has not been plucked by hand, before all the grasses [Col. 1419B] it withers; so is the path of all who forget God, and the hope of the hypocrite will perish. For his folly will not please him, and his confidence is like a spider’s web. He will lean upon his house, and it will not stand; he will prop it up, and it will not rise. He appears moist before the sun comes, and at its rising his shoot will come forth. Its roots will thicken upon a heap of rocks, and it will dwell among stones; if he swallows it up from its place, he will deny it and say: “I do not know you.” For this is the joy of its path, that others may again spring up from the earth. God will not cast away the innocent, nor will he extend his hand to the wicked, until your mouth is filled with laughter and your lips with rejoicing. Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the impious will not endure.

[Col. 1418C] Bildad was offended because Job had said that he was more powerful in the kingdom than the other kings. For by saying “How long?” he shows that he could no longer endure words of exhortation. The justice of God inserts such punishments only into one who is guilty, such as those which you endure. He delivered them into the vengeance of those doing evil to them. He can do you no harm in any way if you rise from the darkness of errors to the knowledge of divine justice. If you are pure in heart and mouth, he will immediately attend to the restoration of your happiness. He will release your body, quiet after the battle of punishments. Riches before the blow, in comparison with glory after the blow: these things, however, apply to penitents [Col. 1419A]. Seek the memory of those whose life is longer, and you will learn that some perished by the flood and others by sulfur. We have existed only a short time, and do not endure for long. The wicked in the present age had different kinds of death. These are certainly the deeds of people of former times. Now he speaks openly about Job. Thus you too could not remain in your former happiness without righteousness. As grass withers in summer, so he reproaches holy Job with deserving to perish before sinners. [Col. 1419B] Because God sees into all things. Those who pretend to holiness of life will perish. Pretense is compared with folly, which is certainly destroyed by a slight breath of air. By trusting in himself, he does not rise by his own strength, because the Lord is not his strength. He who appears to stand in prosperity is broken by tribulations. At first he appears to prosper, but he does not endure. There, lacking the moisture of life, he will die without the fruit of works. By the likeness of a living thing he will be reckoned among the hard-hearted. From the present [Col. 1419C] age—that is, God. Through wicked arts. It is read as spoken ironically. For when the impious has been cast down, the righteous is raised up. He looks upon the humble; he will not give help. That is, to spirits. He indicates joy of heart, a voice of exultation. Sinners and demons. For lovers of the world are suddenly taken away from the age.

## CHAPTER IX

[Col. 1419D] Job answered and said: Truly I know that it is so, that a human being compared with God will not be justified. If he wishes to contend with him, he will not be able to answer him one thing out of a thousand. He is wise in heart and strong in power; who has resisted him and had peace? Who has moved mountains, and they did not know it, those whom he overturned in his anger? He shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars tremble. He commands the sun, and it does not rise; and he seals up the stars [Col. 1420A] as though under a seal. He alone stretches out the heavens and walks upon the waves of the sea. He makes Arcturus, Orion, and the Hyades, and the inner chambers of the south. He does great and incomprehensible and wondrous things, whose number there is none. If he comes to me, I will not see him; if he departs, I will not understand him. If he suddenly questions, who will answer him? Or who can say: “Why do you do this?” God, whose anger no one can resist, and beneath whom those who bear up the world bend [Col. 1420B]. How great, then, am I, that I should answer him and speak with him in my words? Even if I have something just to say, I will not answer, but I will supplicate my judge. And when he has heard me calling, I do not believe that he has heard my voice. For in a whirlwind he will crush me and multiply my wounds even without cause. He does not permit my spirit to rest [Col. 1420C], and he fills me with bitterness. If strength is sought, he is the strongest. If equity of judgment is sought, no one dares to testify on my behalf. If I wish to justify myself, my mouth will condemn me; if I wish to show myself innocent, it will prove me perverse. And if I am upright, my soul itself will not know this, and I shall be weary of my life. There is one thing that I have said: he himself consumes both the innocent and the impious. If he scourges, let him kill once [Col. 1420D], and let him not laugh at the punishments of the innocent. The earth has been given into the hand of the impious; he covers the face of its judges. But if it is not he, who then is it [Al. “who then would it be”]? My days were swifter than a runner; they fled and did not see good. They passed like ships carrying fruit, like an eagle flying toward food. When I say: “I shall not speak in this way,” I change my face and am tortured by grief. I feared all [Col. 1421A] my works, knowing that you would not spare the delinquent. But if I am impious even in this way, why have I labored in vain? If I wash myself as with snow-water, and my hands shine as though most pure, nevertheless you will plunge me into filth, and my garments will abhor me. For I will not answer a man who is like me, nor one who could be heard with me on equal terms in judgment. There is no one who can rebuke both and place his hand [Col. 1421B] upon them both. Let him remove his rod from me, and let his terror not frighten me. I shall speak and shall not fear him, for while afraid I cannot answer.

[Col. 1419C] Bildad had reproached holy Job because he had flattered himself about his holiness [Col. 1419D] and innocence; and Job begins to answer him in this way. One subjected to God receives justice; one placed in opposition loses it. He speaks for the whole human race. Whoever acts against the Lord does not stir up against himself the warfare of his anger? The proud and arrogant in mind, who, because they did not know God, were overthrown on account of their unbelief. The people of the Jews, from their homeland. Priests or judges. At the coming of night. At the coming of [Col. 1420A] day. In these things he shows the Creator’s power. In these stars he indicates that the whole army of the stars belongs to God’s governance. The innermost choirs of angels. In no former ages was it conceivable that a human being, earth, and ashes should be joined to the assemblies of angels. I will not see him with bodily eyes, because he is spirit, if he does not present himself to my presence. If he suddenly summons us to judgment, creation will tremble. Severity is demonstrated by anger. Those who endure the cares of the present [Col. 1420B] age bend by failing. What are the words of a worm and ashes in comparison with divine utterances? I will not glory in my righteousness, but I will supplicate my judge to be favorable. He speaks of the future judgment, in which even the elect will tremble. The devil is understood. The devil adds punishment beyond one’s merits. This happened to him because of a certain sickness. As he says above [Col. 1420C]: No one can resist his anger. Because he knows all things. Because no one lives in the flesh without corruption. If I consider myself harmless. Because he knows better. For the affliction of the present blow, testing one and punishing another. He does not permit the devil to laugh. His flesh obscures wisdom for the adversary [Col. 1420D], so that the judges of the earth may not recognize the truth. God alone conquers adversaries. The days of my happiness: the recompense of merits. That which carries fruit carries food for others, and uses only its fragrance for itself. Thus my happiness has departed. He reproves himself for speaking carelessly about obscure matters. I shall bring forth sad words of bitterness. Because all things [Col. 1421A] will be preserved uncertain for the future. That is, if you wish to investigate me completely, I shall be found unclean. Either in the brightness of innocence or of grace. Because as long as we are clothed with this corruption, we are not fully pure. My body made me unclean. He is God; I am a human being. Because a judge is better than the one who is to be judged. Who can rebuke powerful God as though he were unjust? Because he appeared as both human and God. The blow of correction. Then I shall be able to answer if you remove these two things from me—that is, the hand of power and the rod of correction.

## CHAPTER X

My soul is weary of my life; I shall let my speech loose against myself. I shall speak in the bitterness of my soul; I shall say to God: Do not condemn me; tell me [Col. 1421C] why you judge me so. Does it seem good to you if you accuse me falsely and oppress the work of your hands, and assist the counsel of the impious? Do you have eyes of flesh [Vulg. “fleshy eyes”], or will you see as a human being sees? Are your days like human days, and your years like human times, that you seek out my iniquity and scrutinize my sin? [Col. 1421D] And you will know that I have done nothing impious, although there is no one who can rescue himself from your hand. Your hands made me and fashioned me entirely round about; and do you suddenly cast me down in this way? Remember, I beg you, that you made me like clay and will reduce me to dust. Did you not milk me like milk and coagulate me like cheese? You clothed me with skin and flesh, and joined me together with bones and sinews [Col. 1422A]. You granted me life and mercy, and your visitation guarded my spirit. Although you hide these things in your heart, nevertheless I know that you remember all things. If I sinned and you spared me for a time, why do you not allow me to be cleansed from my iniquity? And if I am impious, woe is me; and if I am righteous, I shall not lift up my head, filled with affliction and misery. And because of pride [Col. 1422B] you will seize me like a lioness; and, turning back, you torture me wondrously and renew your witnesses against me. You multiply your anger against me, and punishments wage war against me. Why did you bring me out of the womb? Would that I had been consumed, so that no eye might see me. I would have been as though I had never existed, carried from the womb to the tomb. Will not the small number of my days soon come to an end? Leave me, then, so that I may mourn my pain for a little while [Col. 1422C], before I go and do not return to the land of darkness, covered by the gloom of death; to the land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death, no order, and everlasting horror dwell.

[Col. 1421B] This verse was discussed above. Whoever speaks against God speaks against himself. Let bitterness punish whatever the tongue accuses through the judgment of the mind. He says this out of confidence in his righteousness, because he did not yet know God’s hidden judgment. That is: You who punish in this way here, show me why, so that I may go there secure. He does not affirm this meaning, but weakens it by examining and denying it. Demons, or Job’s friends. Your judgment does not err as human judgments do. Do the days of your eternity end like human days? With the greatest care you seek the reasons by which to take vengeance on me. Why do you question my faults with blows, though you did not fail to know me before you formed me? Spare me, [Col. 1421D] Lord, because no power can withstand you. In the hands we understand the divine operation, because the human being was formed from clay. He speaks against those who say that one Lord is the Creator of the soul and another of the body. He desires the Creator’s mercy, displaying the frail material of the flesh. By this likeness he shows that, in the wombs of mothers, divinity performs the creation of the human being. You leave me outside for testing, but inwardly you nevertheless guard me, binding me to your powers so that I do not perish [Col. 1422A]. That is, the soul, which gives life to human beings. For this reason God visits, so that he may guard those whom he visits with protection. These things you bestowed upon me from the beginning, but you seem to conceal them from me, while you leave me to be crushed in every way. If once I committed some offense and you did not seek vengeance, your indulgence ought to have continued. If pardon removed the guilt, why did it not erase it from memory? If I am righteous, it is the same as though I were impious, because I endure the weight of punishments owed to the impious. You liken a humble human being to the most savage beasts. You add old punishments to new ones [Col. 1422B]. You allow adversaries to rage, who have testified that I am worthy of punishments. Vengeance. The wicked exercise cruelty. He already said this at the beginning: Why did I not die in the womb? He also said earlier: Like a hidden premature child, I would not have endured. The days of my life, which have now passed in a brief span, I do not spend without torments. Grant me rest. The merits of offenses, or the pain of punishments. That he described the land [Col. 1422C] of the underworld is beyond doubt—not that the one who mourns his guilt will go to the dark land, but that the one who neglects to mourn will undoubtedly go there.

## CHAPTER XI

Then Sophar the Naamathite answered and said: Will one who speaks much not be heard, or will a verbose man be justified? Will people be silent only for you? And when you have mocked everyone else, will no one refute you? For you said: “My speech is pure and clean [Vulg. ‘I am clean’] in your sight.” Would that God himself spoke with you and opened his lips to you, so that he might show you the secrets of wisdom and how manifold his law is! Then you would understand that much less is demanded of you by God than your iniquity deserved. Perhaps you will comprehend the footprints of God and discover the Almighty to perfection [Col. 1423A]. He is higher than heaven—what will you do? Deeper than hell—whence will you know? His measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea. If he overturns all things or confines them into one, who will contradict him? For he knows human vanity, and when he sees iniquity, does he not consider it? A vain man is raised up in pride and thinks himself born free, like a wild donkey’s colt. But you have made your heart firm and spread out your hands toward God. If you remove from yourself the iniquity that is in your hand and injustice has not remained in your tent, then you will be able to lift your face without stain and will be stable and unafraid [Col. 1423B]. You will also forget misery and remember it like waters that have passed away. At evening a brightness like midday will rise for you, and when you think yourself consumed, you will rise [Col. 1423C] like Lucifer. You will have confidence in the hope set before you, and, having searched around, you will sleep securely and rest. There will be no one to terrify you, and very many will entreat your face. But the eyes of the impious will fail, refuge will perish from them, and their hope will be an abomination to their soul.

[Col. 1422C] He began to speak to Job with insults. As though he had said: Can a verbose man receive praise, when, because of his excessive verbosity, he is idle in the offense it causes? In this way he attacks holy Job, as though he were about to say great and lofty things. Therefore these are the words of an accuser, not of one pursuing truth and justice. In speaking he wished to indicate the voice of God, as though he were saying: I pity your ignorance rather than your punishment. That he should grant understanding of his voice. The hidden and remote judgments of his heart, in which his law is manifold and inscrutable. You will understand this if you attend to his judgments. Just as God is invisible, so also he is incomprehensible. [Col. 1423A] We believe that God is everywhere and that all things created by him are contained within him. In these words he says that God is everywhere, and he accuses holy Job of suffering punishments deservedly and of criticizing God’s judgments. As he destroyed the world in the flood and the Egyptians beneath the waters. In this sense he says that God both observes and punishes those who act wickedly. Vanity casts a shadow. He wishes every kind of wicked person to be understood, one who is not accustomed to the discipline of the strap. You have hardened yourself so as not to repent. [Col. 1423B] False works of merit. Possessing a holy conscience, you raise your face freely to supplicate. In this confidence you will indeed be firm before God and steadfast. The present life, because the more someone desires heavenly things, the more fully he forgets earthly things. At the completion of your labors, Christ, the sun of justice, will come to you as consolation. After death you will rise to glory, because after the blow you will be able to be restored. [Col. 1423C] Because the righteous walks confidently like a lion and will fear no encounter. For the more fully each person casts away from himself the fear that comes from the world, the more truly he conquers the world’s desire within himself. Hypocrites desire to appear as intercessors for human beings. The impulses of bodily desires. That is, the honor and riches of the present life.

## CHAPTER XII

Then Job answered and said: Are you alone human beings, and will wisdom die with you? Nevertheless, know that I have a heart as you do [Vulg. “And I have a heart as you do”], and I am not inferior to you. Who does not know these things that you know? The one who is mocked by his friend, as I am, will call upon God, and he will hear him. The simplicity of the just is mocked. A lamp despised in the thoughts of the rich, prepared for the appointed time [Col. 1424A]. The tents of robbers abound, and they boldly provoke God, although he has given everything into their hands. Surely, ask the beasts, and they will teach you; and the birds of heaven will tell you. Speak to the earth, and it will answer you; and the fish of the sea will recount it to you. Who does not know that the hand of the Lord made all these things, in whose hand is the soul of every living thing and the spirit of all human flesh? Does not the ear distinguish words, and the palate of the eater [Col. 1424B] taste? In the aged is wisdom, and in length of time understanding [Vulg. “prudence”]. With him are wisdom and strength; he possesses counsel and understanding. If he destroys, no one can build. If he shuts a man in, no one can open. If he restrains the waters, all things dry up; if he releases them, they overturn the earth. With him are strength and wisdom; he knows both the deceiver and the one deceived. He brings counselors to a foolish end and judges to bewilderment. He loosens the belt of kings and girds their loins with a rope. He leads priests away inglorious and overthrows nobles. He changes the speech of the truthful and takes away the teaching of the elders. He pours contempt upon princes and raises up those who had been oppressed. He reveals deep things from darkness and brings the shadow of death into the light. [Col. 1424D] He multiplies nations and destroys them, and restores the overthrown to wholeness. He changes the heart of the leaders of the people of the earth and deceives them so that they proceed in vain. They will grope along an impassable way as in darkness and not in light, and he will make them wander like drunkards.

[Col. 1423C] I wonder why you think that you alone are human beings [Col. 1423D] and possess wisdom, so that it cannot extend to others. Thus I know as you do. Who is there who can or ought to be ignorant of these things you say about God’s greatness or justice? This is manifest in holy Job according to the literal sense. Christ’s simplicity was mocked by the Jews. He is certainly designating the proud, who despised him while he was afflicted, whom glory [Col. 1424A] will reveal on the day of recompense. The Sabaeans and Chaldaeans abound in his riches. For the wicked grow more arrogant against the Lord the more they are exalted in the honor of the world. That all things belong to God’s governance—even irrational and senseless things—which, when questioned in accordance with the manner of truth, answer in a certain way. In the divine power, in which all the saints are specially contained. By the ears, words are understood. The palates of those who eat receive and discern taste. [Col. 1424B] He alone truly knows by what judgment and justice he distributes all things, who in Daniel is called the Ancient of Days. Whatever he wishes to destroy by the judgment of his wisdom, who will be able to resist? No one will be able to free one confined in hell. Spiritually, the waters of teachings are contained among the Jewish peoples and are dried up, while the earth of the Church advances in spiritual life; according to the literal sense, this is manifest. Christ is the wisdom of God the Father, and the Holy Spirit is strength. As happened with Ahab and his prophets. As we read happened in Egypt concerning Pharaoh’s counselors and magicians. The glory of the reigning person is understood. The disgrace of one deposed from the kingdom. He will surround their loins with the rope of sins. As is written in the Books of Kings concerning the priests Saraiah and Sophonia: He removes the wicked and establishes the righteous. When the righteous sins, the glory of his lips is changed. The elders and judges of the Jews. As Saul was rejected and disapproved by God. As David was raised to the kingdom, while previously he had endured Saul’s persecutions. He disclosed the mysteries of the law. Sinners into the light of faith. Growing daily through the flesh. When they depart from the world. They will be restored in the resurrection. He permits them to be deceived, or compels them to deceive in accordance with the demerit of their iniquities. That is, they think they walk by their own invention, but they err; because one who is unwilling to see the light must wander in darkness. Now here, now there the drunkard proceeds: so do the Jews, blinded in mind.

## CHAPTER XIII

My eye has seen all these things [Vulg. “Behold, my eye has seen all things”], and my ear has heard them, and I have understood each one according to your knowledge. And I know also, and I am not inferior to you. Nevertheless, I shall speak to the Almighty, and I desire to dispute with the Lord. First I shall show you to be fabricators of lies and worshipers of perverse doctrines. Would that you were silent, so that you might be thought wise! Hear, therefore, my rebukes, and attend to the judgment of my lips [Col. 1425B]. Does God need your lie, so that you may speak deceitfully on his behalf? Will you show partiality to him and endeavor to judge on God’s behalf? Or will the one whom nothing can escape be pleased with it? Or will he be deceived like a human being by your frauds? He himself will reprove you. In secret [Vulg. “He himself will reprove you, because secretly…”] you accept his person. As soon as he is moved, he will disturb you, [Col. 1425C] and his terror will fall upon you. Your memory will be compared with ashes, and your necks will be reduced to clay. Be silent for a little while, so that I may speak briefly what my mind has suggested. Why do I tear my flesh with my teeth and carry my soul in my hands? Even if he kills me, I shall hope in him. Nevertheless, I shall defend my ways before him, and he himself will be my Savior. For no hypocrite will come into his presence. Hear [Col. 1425D] my speech and receive the riddles with your ears. If I am judged, I know that I shall be found righteous. Who is he who will judge with me [Vulg. “who will be judged with me”]? Let him come. Why, while silent, am I consumed? Do not do only two things to me, and then I shall not hide from your face. Put your hand far from me, and let your fear not terrify me. Then call me, and I shall answer you; [Col. 1426A] or certainly I shall speak, and you answer me. Show me how many iniquities I have, and my crimes and my sins and my offenses. Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy? Against a leaf carried by the wind you display your power, and you pursue dry straw. For you write bitter things against me and wish to consume me for the sins of my youth. You have put my foot in the stocks [Col. 1426B], observed all my paths, and examined the traces of my feet. I am to be consumed like rot and like a garment eaten by the moth.

[Col. 1424D] The eye of my mind, which is the lamp of my body, saw [Col. 1425A] all these things that I have recounted, with the Lord revealing them. Since I am not more foolish than you, I shall supplicate his mercy. To dispute with God is to submit one’s life to an examination under such investigation of his justice. While you assert that I deserve to suffer all these things, because you say that no one endures such evils as I do unless his merits demand them. This is manifest. In what follows he recounts the same rebukes one by one. Because they were deceitfully devising things under words of consolation. As though he were saying: Do you think that you ought to flatter God deceitfully [Col. 1425B]? Have you assumed the role of judge against me, so that, as though you were God, you may condemn me by your sentence as deserving it? Can you impose this unjust understanding of yours upon the one to whom everything is open, as though he were ignorant of human hearts and could therefore judge me incorrectly? You deserve to be reproved by God. Or, in examining judgments that are hidden, you wish to assume the person of God, to whom this alone belongs.

So that you ought to flatter him in your heart. The movement of God is called the just strictness of his judgment. Human mortality [Col. 1425C] will be compared with ashes. Pride is recognized in the neck. Since he himself was placed in sufferings, he asks for silence so that he may speak. Perhaps because of excessive pain he was tearing his own flesh. That is, my life, which is often used in place of the word “soul.” As he says elsewhere: Until I fail, I will not depart from my innocence. This will come to me for salvation, when he has rendered my ways purified by correction. But who are you, that you presume to rebuke me as though you were righteous? [Col. 1425D] Because they did not understand that the righteous are afflicted, he called them riddles. I say to you: I have no basis for being condemned; he did not say this concerning God’s judgment. Let this speech not be counted arrogance, but confidence in a good conscience. Why was I not heard beforehand, and if I had been guilty, why would I then be consumed? This is the whole matter that holy Job asks of God: first to remove the blow from him, and then the divine power, which he could not endure. As though placed face to face on equal terms, he says to him [Col. 1426A] why he must endure the temptation inflicted upon him. In these names of crimes and offenses, blessed Job signifies great and small sins, which he asks to have shown to him so that he may understand the cause of the blow. I know that your present visitation and protection are present, but you hide them from me while permitting me to be punished in this way. He considers within himself what he is in relation to God and compares himself with the most worthless things. He called the exceedingly bitter torments that he endured by God’s permission “bitterness.” He supplicates for the offenses and ignorances of youth. To place one’s foot in the stocks is to bind all a person’s ways with severe strictness. Because he carefully examines each and every small deed of a human being [Col. 1426B]. He indicates that he has a prolonged tribulation of the blow, since long-lasting decay has consumed him.

## CHAPTER XIV

A man born of woman, living for a short time, will be filled with many miseries. Like a flower he will come forth and be crushed; he flees like a shadow and never remains in the same condition. [Col. 1426C] And do you consider it worthy to open your eyes upon such a one and bring him with you into judgment? Who can make clean what was conceived from unclean seed? Is it not you alone? The days of a human being are short; the number of his months is with you. You have appointed his boundaries, which cannot be passed. Withdraw from him for a little while, so that he may rest, until his desired day comes like that of a hired laborer. A tree has hope: if it is cut down, [Col. 1426D] it grows green again, and its branches sprout. If its root has aged in the earth and its trunk has died in the dust, at the scent of water it will bud and produce a crown of foliage, as when it was first planted. But when a human being has died, been stripped, and consumed, where, I ask, is he? As waters depart from the sea and a river, emptied, dries up, so a human being, when he sleeps, will not rise again. [Col. 1427A] Until heaven is worn away, he will not awaken or rise from his sleep. Who will grant me this: that you protect me in the underworld and hide me until your fury passes, and appoint a time for me when you will remember me? Do you think that a dead human being will live again? All the days in which I now serve as a soldier, I await until my transformation comes. You will call me, and I shall answer you; [Col. 1427B] you will extend your right hand to the work of your hands. You have indeed counted my steps, but you spare my sins. You sealed up my offenses as though in a bag, but you healed my iniquity. A mountain will fall, collapsing [Vulg. “falling, it is destroyed”], and a rock will be moved from its place. Waters hollow out stones, and by their overflow the earth is gradually consumed. So, then, you will likewise destroy a human being. You strengthened him for a little while, so that he might pass away forever. You will change his face [Col. 1427C] and [absent in the Vulgate] will not release him. Whether his children are noble or ignoble, he will not know. Nevertheless, while his flesh lives, it will grieve, and his soul will mourn over itself.

[Col. 1426B] The human race is said to have been lost in Adam and filled with many miseries. Here we understand the frailty of the human race: because every day we grow, or diminish at every moment. He opened the eyes of compassion upon the human race, so that he might restore it [Col. 1426C] in Christ. The saints will judge, as it is said to the Apostles: “You will sit upon thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Matthew 19:28). In the Spirit he foretold our future reconciliation in Christ. “The measure of their end”: my days have received it, so that they may not exceed the limit of their completion. Remove the scourges of the present life. Show the good things of eternal rest. “Man’s departure from the world,” that is, from the present life. Through the resurrection the body comes back to life. [Col. 1426D] “Holy hearers”: those who follow examples of good works. When Adam grows old in sins, and every good thing of nature that he possessed, having died beforehand to its greenness, revives again at the scent of the water of baptism, it puts forth leaves again, as when it was first planted in paradise. A wicked man removed from the present life undoubtedly goes into destruction. The world is compared with the sea; when the soul has been withdrawn, the body remains empty. [Col. 1427A] He says that the airy heaven will perish, and then foretells that the human body will rise again, because no one ascended into heaven before Christ’s coming. Severity against sinners. Until Christ redeems us, I beg that you protect me from the ministers of hell. He assumes the sentence of the weak. For just as one who sweats in battle has uncertain outcomes, so it is doubtful with what end the labor of the present life will close. “Teaching what belongs to the law”: by fulfilling the commandments. For no one can be saved without this right hand, that is, the Son of God. [Col. 1427B] You mark each work for retribution. You forgive sins to the penitent. For the sins of human beings, unless they have been erased by repentance, are kept in secrecy and for judgment. So that the saints may often be changed from the state of righteousness and transferred to iniquity. Those hard of heart are deceived by evil spirits through subtle temptation. By a just judgment you permit the one who seemed to himself to stand upright to be tested. For the present life is brief. Into joy or punishment. When by death you crush his appearance. Toward the things he thinks he will obtain. Not this is understood of carnal nobility, but of spiritual nobility. It is not yet understood from works and conduct who is noble or ignoble. We understand the statement as referring to that which is the first nobility. While he does not know whether his works are approved or even rejected. For no one properly possesses joy in himself; one must rejoice in the Lord.

## CHAPTER XV

Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: “Will a wise man answer as though speaking into the wind, and fill [Col. 1427D] his stomach with burning? You rebuke with words one who is not your equal, and you say what is not advantageous to you. As far as you are concerned, you have emptied yourself of fear and have removed prayers from before God.
