Your iniquity has taught your mouth, and you imitate the tongue of blasphemers. Your mouth will condemn you, and not I; your lips will answer you. Were you the first [Col. 1428A] man born, and were you formed before the hills? Have you heard the counsel of God, and is his wisdom inferior to you? What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not? Among us are both old men and ancient men, much older than your fathers. Is it a great thing that God should console you? But your perverse words prevent this. What lifts up your heart? And why, as though devising great things, do you keep your eyes fixed in astonishment? Why does your spirit swell up against [Col. 1428B] God, so that you utter such words from your mouth? What is man, that he should be without stain, and that one born of a woman should appear righteous? Behold, among his holy ones there is none unchangeable; behold, the heavens are not clean in his sight. How much more abominable and changeable [Vulgate: useless] is man, who drinks iniquities like water! I will show you; listen to me. I will recount what I have seen. The wise confess and do not [Col. 1428C] conceal their fathers. To them the land was given, and no stranger passed among them. All his days the wicked man is arrogant, and the number of his years is uncertain because of his tyranny. The sound of terror [not found in the Vulgate] is always in his ears, and when there is peace he suspects ambushes. He does not believe that he can return from darkness [Vulgate adds: to the light], looking all around for the sword. When he moves to seek bread, he knows that the day of darkness is ready in his hand. Tribulation will terrify him, and anguish will surround him, like a king preparing for battle. For he stretched out his hand against God and strengthened himself against the Almighty. He ran against him with his neck erect and armed with a fat neck. His fatness covered his face, and his layers of fat hung from his sides. [Col. 1429A] He will dwell in desolate cities and in deserted houses that have been reduced to a heap. He will not become rich, nor will his substance endure, nor will he send his root into the earth. He will not withdraw from darkness. A flame will dry up his branches. The breath of his mouth [Vulgate: of his own mouth] will be taken away. Let him not, deceived by a vain error, believe that he can be redeemed at any price. Before his days [Col. 1429B] are fulfilled, he will perish, and his hand will wither. His cluster will be damaged like a vine in its first flowering, and like an olive tree casting off its blossom. For the assembly of the hypocrite is barren, and fire will devour the tents of those who gladly accept gifts. He conceived pain and gave birth to iniquity, and his womb prepared deceit.”

[Col. 1427C] He rebukes holy Job for speaking vainly in pride. He wished to indicate his mind, since he had dared to grow angry against God as though against an equal, in the gall of anger. In these words blessed Job is reproved by Eliphaz. You are so puffed up that you are empty of divine fear and disdain praying to the Lord. What he utters with his mouth is conceived from an evil way. You are a disciple of those who blaspheme God. You will receive the merits of your words. Since you savor earthly things, why do you speak about eternal things? Before all angelic creatures. He vehemently rebuked holy Job because he thought he possessed the counsel of God and that divine wisdom was inferior to him. He knew Christ himself more deeply and saw the mysteries through the Spirit. These men differ greatly in knowledge from your fathers, whose evil conduct you imitate as an evil son. If you corrected your profession of faith, the scourges would long ago have ceased. By understanding and thought he designates him as speaking proudly and vainly. [Col. 1428B] He spoke these things in anger because Job had said earlier: “If I am judged, I know that I shall be found righteous.” For he found wickedness among the former angels. The saints are so considered in comparison with him. He reproaches holy Job as abominable and useless to God without works. A fool sins without reflection, as though swallowing a drink. Know that I have learned by experience what I speak. They do not defend themselves or their fathers, who are like them. [Col. 1428C] He speaks of heretics, who believe that they alone know the mysteries. “The saints” are to be understood as those alien to heretics. The perverse teacher, or the devil. He says this concerning his pride. Because the devil knows that the judgment of his destruction is destined for him: here the devil and his entire body are understood. The wicked man despairs that he can return to repentance. Expecting death for himself from every side. The sinner seeking the wages of the present life. Nothing else [Col. 1428D] comes to the devil’s mind except that terrifying time of God’s judgment, when he fears that perpetual punishments will be imposed upon him. He will be confined by pressures because of fear of punishments. He signifies the devil, or the wicked man who prepares the wars of vices in opposition to God. By the raising or spreading out of the hand, he shows one resisting God. He says that he has been strengthened according to the merits of his obstinacy. The devil or the wicked man hastens boldly to perpetrate those things that displease God. He indicates overflowing pride. His sins darken the mind of the soul. [Col. 1429A] The ministers of the devil, from whom the arrogance of the mind hangs. Among the thoughts of the wicked. The assemblies of the wicked are called desolate because they do not have God as an inhabitant. While indeed he gathers what will perish. Since he himself will quickly be punished. Of the living. The memory, so that he may hope for future things. From unbelief to repentance. His followers and evil works. Of tribulation. His counsel will not endure. The wicked man will not be redeemed at any price; or, the devil will not be redeemed from the destruction of perdition. Before the day of judgment, foreknown [Col. 1429B] in predestination, he will perish. The life of the wicked does not grow, but withers either from the heat of pride or from the coldness of love for God. The people of the Jews, rejecting Christ, the most chaste blossom. In these words he falsely marks holy Job as a robber and deceiver, and says that riches gathered through iniquity will benefit him nothing. He wishes human praise to be understood. When he conceives something perverse. When he strives to fulfill it. The mind of a wicked man may be understood, since it does not cease preparing deceits.

## CHAPTER XVI

[Col. 1429C] Then Job answered and said: “I have often heard such things; all of you are burdensome comforters. Will windy words have an end, or is anything troublesome to you if you speak? I also could speak things like yours. Would that your soul were in place of my soul! I too would comfort you with words and shake my head over you. I would strengthen you with my mouth, and I would move my lips as though sparing you. [Col. 1429D] But what shall I do? If I speak, my pain does not rest; and if I am silent, it does not depart from me. Now my pain has overwhelmed me, and my limbs have been reduced to nothing. My wrinkles testify against me, and a liar rises up against my soul, contradicting me. He has gathered his fury against me, and threatening me, he gnashes his teeth against me. [Col. 1430A] My enemy has looked upon me with terrible eyes; they have opened their mouths against me, and reproaching me, they have struck my cheek; they have been sated with my sufferings. God has confined me with the wicked and delivered me into the hands of the unjust. I, once wealthy, have suddenly been crushed. He seized my neck and broke me and set me up for himself [Col. 1430B] as though for a target. He surrounded me with his spears; he wounded my loins repeatedly; he did not spare me and poured out my entrails upon the ground. He cut me down, wound upon wound; he rushed upon me like a giant. He sewed sackcloth upon my skin and covered my flesh with ashes. My face swelled from weeping, and my eyelids grew dark. I have suffered these things [Col. 1430C] without iniquity in my hands, though I had pure prayers before God. Earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry find no place of concealment in you. For behold, my witness is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high. My friends are wordy; my eye drips toward God. Would that a man might be judged with God as a son of man is judged with his companion! For behold, the brief years pass, and I walk paths by which I shall not return.”

[Col. 1429C] He received such insults either from his friends or from others. “An end”: that is, either a limit or a method—namely, vanity. It is not troublesome to the speaker, although injurious loquacity is more burdensome to the hearer than to the one speaking. This is evident. If you suffered what I suffer, I would not act toward you as you act toward me. I would confirm over you the soothing affection of my mind. I would bring forth consoling words. I would moderate my speech, showing the affection of one who sympathizes. How could I express compassion? Whether I speak or remain silent, I am tormented by unceasing pain. The calamity of the wound. He cries out that he has been overcome and oppressed by the calamities of the wound he was suffering. The defilements of madness that I endure, and the dust, declare how great the torments are that I suffer. He speaks of Eliphaz himself, or of the devil, because he could not prove what he had said to the Lord: “Touch his bone and his flesh,” and the rest. He poured out the indignation of a raging spirit. Through the mouths of the friends disputing against holy Job, the devil threatened. [Col. 1430A] He calls him the devil, who aroused terrifying images for him in sleep, saying what Tobias later heard: “Where are your righteous deeds now? Behold what you suffer.” While they cast reproaches and curses into his face. A wicked spirit is said in a certain way to be satiated when it sees those whom it hates undeservedly being tormented. When the flesh of a saint is handed over to persecution. He was delivered into the hands of the wicked, whom the devil incites. He had been extremely rich and a powerful king, but suddenly, with the Lord permitting it, he was deprived of all his resources. It signifies the lifting up of his strength and freedom. If he had any pride. Just as archers shoot arrows at a target, so the devil sent the darts of temptations against blessed [Col. 1430B] Job. He speaks of every kind of temptation by the devil. He had not merely rotted externally in his body; internally as well, he melted entirely in the foul discharge of his corruption. Adding wounds to wounds. While countless sores add themselves to my illnesses and wounds, I am divided and wholly dissolved. He spoke not plainly but from the sense of his humiliation. “I have become,” he says, “an object of contempt and disdain to all.” For he had greater grief in his pain. He refers to the dimness of the eyes, since the eyelids are said to flutter. He demonstrates the cause of his innocence, because the Lord had praised him. [Col. 1430C] By the name of blood he means the condition of the present life, so that the merit of the innocent may not remain hidden. In the cry of one praying to the Lord he indicates his earnestness, or his holiness protesting against the punishment inflicted upon him. It is true that blessed Job had God as the witness and knower of his holy life. Those who speak vainly are called wordy, as these men did against holy Job. Let him weep toward God, since among human beings he has no faithful comfort, through tears. When one contends with a human being, he recognizes what he wants to say and what is said; but one who is scourged by God does not have such recognition. The intervals [Col. 1430D] of the present life. For another life will exist after this one.

## CHAPTER XVII

My spirit will be weakened; my days will be shortened, and only the grave remains for me. I have not sinned, yet my eye remains in bitterness. Set me free and place me beside you, and let anyone’s hand fight against me. You have made their heart far from discipline, [Col. 1431A] and therefore they will not be exalted. He promises prey to his companions, and the eyes of his sons will fail. He has made me as a proverb of the people, and I have become an example before them. My eye has grown dim from indignation, and my limbs have been reduced almost to nothing. The righteous will be astonished at this, and the innocent will rise up against [Col. 1431B] the hypocrite. The righteous will hold to his way, and he whose hands are clean will add strength. Therefore all of you, turn and come, and I shall not find any wisdom in you. My days pass, and my thoughts are scattered, tormenting my heart. They have turned night into day, and again after darkness I hope for light. If I endure, hell is my house; in darkness I have made my bed. I have said to corruption, “You are my father,” and to worms, “My mother and my sister.” Where then is my expectation, and who considers my patience? All that I have descends into the deepest hell; do you suppose that at least there I shall have rest?”

[Col. 1430D] In these words he indicates death, which is already hanging over him. Thus the saints speak, since they always consider the end. By blasphemy against God. Thus the saints become while they remain here. The intention of the mind. Protect me, as Moses was protected by the covering of the rock. The heart of Job’s friends—or of heretics—was made far from discipline by the just judgment of God. The ancient enemy promised prey to evil spirits, that is, the souls of the wicked. For the wicked labor over that which they cannot take with them from the world. As he says elsewhere: “Now the younger in time mock me,” and the rest. Now Job complains that the eyes of his mind have grown dim from the indignation by which the merits of his holiness moved him. Because he suffered punishments with a good conscience. How a righteous man is afflicted with very great punishments. Namely, blessed Job. The devil or Job’s friends, against whom he himself is raised in combat. He says that perseverance in holiness [Col. 1431B] has been strengthened. In good works. The strength of the soul. Turning refers to correction. “Cease from reproving me,” because Job’s friends spoke insulting words against the one whom the Lord had praised. The days of past happiness may be understood. Because of the affliction of the wounds. As I had no rest in day or night, but endured continual vigils through pain. He calls hell a house by comparison with his torments. To spread a bed in darkness is to seek rest amid uncertainty. Thus in my flesh [Col. 1431C] there are worms and corruption, so that I might be born from them as from a parent. In the same sense as he says elsewhere: “I expected good things, and evils came to me.” He shows himself strong amid those torments. He calls “all his things” the soul, in which the whole condition of a human being is contained. If I suffer punishments here, do you suppose that I shall have any rest in places of punishment?

## CHAPTER XVIII

Then Baldad the Shuhite answered and said: “Will you continue to hurl words until the end? Understand first, and then let us speak. Why are we reckoned as beasts [Col. 1431D] and regarded as filthy in your eyes? You who destroy my soul in your fury—will the earth be abandoned because of you, and will the rocks be moved from their place? Will not the light of the wicked be extinguished, nor the flame of his fire shine? Light will grow dark in his tent, and the lamp that is over him will be extinguished. The steps of his strength will be constrained, [Col. 1432A] and his own counsel will cast him down. For he has thrust his feet into a net and walks in his snares [Vulgate: spots]. His heel will be caught in a snare, and thirst will burn against him. His trap is hidden in the earth, and his decoy is over the path. Terrors will frighten him on every side and entangle his feet. His strength will be weakened by hunger, and starvation will invade his ribs. [Col. 1432B] The firstborn of death will devour the beauty of his skin and consume his arms. His confidence will be torn from his tent, and the king of destruction will trample upon him. Let his companions—he who is not—dwell in his tent; let sulfur be scattered in his dwelling [Vulgate: tent]. Below, his roots will be cut off [Vulgate: dried up], and above, his harvest will be destroyed. Let his memory perish from the earth, and let his name not be celebrated in the streets. He will drive him from light into darkness and transfer him from the world. He will have neither seed nor offspring among his people, nor any survivors in his regions. On his day the last will be astonished, and horror will seize the first. These are the tents of the wicked, and this is the place of the one who does not know God.”

[Col. 1431C] He rebukes holy Job for being wordy. As though he were not alone, because he did not cease speaking through his spirit, he spoke in the plural. The vilest [Col. 1431D] and unworthy of conversation. “In the madness of your fury you have brought death upon your soul.” As though he were saying: Is the world not subject to its ruler because of you? The lofty and proud things of the world are understood, which may be called rocks because of worldly honor. He says that blessed Job’s happiness has been extinguished, since he has been deprived of it. He foolishly says that he will not recover his former happiness. Present joy in the thought of his heart. Namely, divine protection. By the straits of tribulations, so that he cannot escape from them at all. [Col. 1432A] A person is most of all deceived by his own counsel when he trusts in his strength. He entangles his paths in the error of sin, in which he becomes ensnared so that he may fall. The end comes from the ancient enemy. The devil, who thirsts for the destruction of the human race. By the decoy in which bait is placed, the delights of the world are signified, since the ignorant pursue them as bait is taken by a trap. The wicked man will be terrified by fear of future punishment. He who is not nourished by spiritual food that proceeds from the mouth of God: the inner senses of the mind. Temporal glory [Col. 1432B] which, while seen externally, is held like beauty in the skin. Pride or the devil supplants the glory of the wicked. Polluted by his sins, let him have no confidence in entreating the Lord. At the end the wicked man is trampled by the devil. The ancient enemy, because he brought destruction. Here he desires demons to be in Job’s house, the ministers of the ancient enemy. He is not, therefore, because he has departed from the highest Essence. The stench of sin in his life. The thoughts of evil people. Their activity is despised by God. Let him lose the height of earthly praise and [Col. 1432C] lose the joy of mammon. From the present life into death. From this world let him be transferred by the heavenly Judge into Tartarus. For the people of the wicked will likewise remain in punishments. Because the strict Judge, together with the end of the world, closes up his iniquities. At the time of condemnation, when the things mentioned above have come, the lowly and the nobles among the wicked will be terrified. For such a place suits the merits of the hypocrite.

## CHAPTER XIX

[Col. 1432D] Job answered and said: “How long will you afflict my soul and crush me with words? Behold, you have confounded me ten times, and you are not ashamed to oppress me. Even if I have been ignorant, my ignorance will remain with me. But you rise up against me and reproach me for my reproaches. At least now understand that God has not afflicted me with an equitable judgment and has surrounded me with his scourges. Behold, I will cry out, suffering violence, [Col. 1433A] and no one will hear; I will shout, and there is no one to judge. He has fenced in my path, and I cannot pass; he has placed darkness in my way. He has stripped me of my glory and taken the crown from my head. He has destroyed me on every side, and I perish; like a tree uprooted, he has taken away my hope. His fury has grown angry against me, and he has treated me as his enemy. His raiders have come together [Col. 1433B] and made a way through me, and they have encircled my tent. He has put my brothers far from me, and my acquaintances have withdrawn from me like strangers. My relatives have abandoned me, and those who knew me have forgotten me. The inhabitants of my house and my maidservants have treated me as a stranger, and I was like a foreigner in their eyes. I called my servant, and he did not answer; I pleaded with him with my own mouth. My wife shuddered at my breath [Col. 1433C], and I entreated the sons of my womb. Even fools despised me, and when I withdrew from them, they spoke against me. My counselors once abhorred me, and the one whom I loved most turned away from me. My mouth has clung to my skin, my flesh having been consumed, and only my lips around my teeth remain. Pity me, pity me [Vulgate adds: me], [Col. 1433D] at least you, my friends, because the hand of the Lord has touched me. Why do you persecute me like God and gorge yourselves on flesh [Vulgate adds: my flesh]? Who will grant that my words be written? Who will grant me that they be inscribed in a book with an iron stylus and a sheet of lead, or carved with a chisel into flint? For I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last [Vulgate adds: day] I shall rise from the earth. And again I shall be clothed with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see God. I myself shall see him, and my eyes shall behold him, and not another. This hope has been placed in my bosom. Why then do you now say: ‘Let us persecute him and find the root of his word against him’? Flee, therefore, from the face of the sword, for the sword is the avenger of iniquities, and know that there is a judgment.”

[Col. 1432D] By counting the words of Job’s friends, we understand that they have spoken five times more; but because he had heard five reproaches from them and had answered each of their reproaches five times, he declares that he has been confounded ten times. If you think that I am ignorant of God. You exalt yourselves proudly, saying that he suffers because of impiety. He says that it is not equitable that such a life should be punished with such scourges. With the blows of punishments. He speaks in the manner of the sick. [Col. 1433A] Therefore the Almighty sometimes pretends not to hear here, so that as temptation increases, merits may increase. Along that path I was progressing rightly. He has shut me in with intolerable pains. He permits the miseries of the wounds. He deprived me of the glory of the kingdom. The confidence of my faith, or the crown of honor. My household, children, and bodily health. I see myself utterly perishing. Even the hope of my life has been taken away from me like an uprooted tree. He calls his pain the fury of God, to whom he is subject. As though I were opposed to his will. The ministers of the devil are designated; they did violence to him and raged cruelly against him. [Col. 1433B] They surround the mind and body with every temptation, because the soul is forbidden to them. He says that God did it because he permitted it to happen. For the Savior also says to the Father in the Psalms: “You have put far from me friend and neighbor,” and so forth. This refers to servants. It is a greater insult when servants despise their masters, who speak gently to them. What happened to blessed Job arose from weakness, so that in speaking he exhaled a foul odor from the purulence of his deep wound. [Col. 1433C] Those whom I nourished with the teaching of wisdom, I entreated to be gracious to me. Hence greater indignation arises, so that fools mock wisdom. This indicates that he did not always sit on the dung heap during his temptation. The Jews: Christ. The assembly of the Jews. It is evident. Among the other evils, this was added, that the skin of my flesh clung to my bones. The devil consumed his entire body with torments, but left his lips so that through them they might stir him to blasphemy in his pain. Offer me the consolation of pitiable compassion. Although others above had also abhorred me. He afflicted me by his power. God’s persecuting is to scourge the saints kindly. Why do you desire punishments for me? Since he could find consolation from no human being, he turned to God and prophesied the future resurrection. Through iron, lead, and flint he shows that the letters would endure in the world, and he desires to be inscribed by them. “I,” he says, “already corrupted by ulcers, shall see God in this mortal flesh, made incorruptible and glorified [Col. 1434A] through the future resurrection.” Certain and unchangeable, he spoke these things upon this foundation of faith. The hope of resurrection: in the secret of the mind. Why do you wish to persecute me as though I believed nothing? To seek the root of a word is to investigate evil in another’s good statement. Withdraw from my oppression so that you may escape the sword, that is, God’s just sentence. Know the judgment of God, by which I shall be able to take vengeance upon my mockers.

## CHAPTER XX

[Col. 1434B] Then Sophar the Naamathite answered and said: “Therefore my thoughts follow one another in confusion, and my mind is carried in different directions, because you assert that you are suffering these evils and punishments while innocent. I will hear the doctrine with which you rebuke me, and the spirit of my understanding will answer you. This I know from the beginning, from the time when man was placed upon the earth: that the praise of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the hypocrite lasts but a moment. If his pride rises up to the heavens [Col. 1434C] and his head touches the clouds, he will perish at the end like a dung heap; and those who saw him will say, ‘Where is he?’ Like a flying dream, he will not be found; he will pass away like a vision of the night. The eye that saw him will not see him, and his place will no longer behold him. His sons will be crushed by poverty, and his hands will repay him for his wrongdoing. His bones will be filled with the vices of his youth, and with him they will sleep [Col. 1434D] in the dust. For when evil is sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue. He will spare it and not abandon it; he will conceal it in his throat. His bread will be changed in his belly into the gall of an asp within him. He will vomit up the riches he swallowed, and God will draw them out of his belly. He will suck the head of an asp, and the tongue of a viper will kill him. [Col. 1435A] He will not see the streams of the river, the torrents of honey and butter. He will pay for all that he has done, yet he will not be consumed. According to the multitude of his inventions, so will he suffer, because, crushing others, he stripped the house of the poor; he seized it [Vulgate: he seized the house of the poor] and did not build it. His belly was not satisfied, and when he has what he desired, he will not be able to possess it. [Col. 1435B] Nothing remained of his food, and therefore nothing of his goods will remain. When he is filled, he will be constricted and will burn, and every pain will rush upon him. May his belly be filled, and may he send upon him the anger of his fury and rain his warfare over him. He will flee iron weapons and rush upon a bronze bow. Drawn out, it goes forth from its sheath and flashes [Col. 1435C] in its bitterness. Terrible things will go and come against him [Vulgate: in his bitterness he goes, and they will come, etc.]. All darkness is hidden in his secret places. Fire that is not kindled will devour him; he will be afflicted, abandoned in his tent. The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him. [Col. 1435D] The offspring of his house will be exposed, and it will be taken away on the day of the Lord’s fury. This is the portion of the wicked man from God, and the inheritance of his words from the Lord.”

[Col. 1434B] “For this reason,” he says, “I am disturbed in my thoughts, because you say that you are suffering these evils without cause from God, the just judge.” As though he were saying: I hear your words, but I shall discern with the spirit of my understanding whether they are so. He marks holy Job as wicked and hypocritical because he was rebellious against God, pretended to be righteous, and now has become rebellious against God; he reproaches him as proud. The elevation of the mind. Through [Col. 1434C] all his wounds he has become putrefied and is compared with a dung heap. Those who knew him in his kingdom will say with an insulting voice: “Where is the most powerful of kings?” Because of the very brief outcome of life. What is the place of the hypocrite except the heart of flatterers? Wherever favors are found, there his heart rests. By God’s sentence they will be consumed in the most miserable poverty. For he will receive condemnation according to the works of his hands. For the beginning of his lust, which is called youth, grows strong through habitual practice. For these vices do not leave him until death. For the iniquity of the hypocrite is the sweetness of his heart: speaking gently, he preserves harshness in his heart. For he does not punish this in himself; he hides it in his mind. The satiety of temporal love, which turns into bitterness at the end, when it is finally recognized as the devil’s persuasion. Divine knowledge, which the wicked sometimes desire to know; but since they refuse to practice it, they vomit it out, and what he had unjustly taken away will certainly be extracted from the wicked man. By the asp is signified the devil’s perverse and hidden persuasion; by the viper, the devil’s open temptation. [Col. 1435A] The gifts of the Holy Spirit are not seen by hypocrites. By these names he signifies the abundance of Paradise. He receives according to everything he has done. Gehenna of fire. As the Prophet says: “For you will repay each according to his works.” He has stated the reasons why the wicked man deserves to pay the punishments mentioned above. In these words he calls holy Job insatiable in desire. Just as you yourself lost your patrimony by a just judgment. Because he did not feed guests from his table or receive strangers; therefore nothing of his goods will remain, that is, of his wealth. For the greater the things he acquires in the world, the more intolerable the straits he suffers in trying to preserve what he has found. He calls the capacity of the soul its belly, so that blasphemy may be heaped up to the very top of his mouth. He calls the devil’s fury and savagery anger. Let him receive strict retribution, tormented by the arrows of temptation drop by drop. When he thinks he can escape lighter calamities, let him fall into more severe ones. Every necessity may suitably be called iron, because it tortures the life of the poor with the wound of sorrow. This bow is understood as the devil. From the underworld. Because he presses inhumanely upon the one whom he has corrupted. Because he pretends to be an angel of light. The companions of the adversary prince burn. The wicked hide their sins in their hearts and take great delight in them. Vengeance that always burns and consumes everything cast into it. Because the wicked man, abandoned by God in a just judgment, will be punished together with his body. The saints or angels reveal the works of the wicked. For earthly things testify against him. The thoughts that previously he alone knew are exposed. Of the mind or intention. On the day of judgment he will be cast into the outer darkness. The recompense of all works. In all these things he had marked holy Job as wicked.

## CHAPTER XXI
Responding, Job said:

“Listen, I beg you, to my words, and repent. Bear with me, so that I too may speak; and afterward, if it seems appropriate, laugh at my words. Is my argument against a human being, so that I should not rightly be grieved? Attend to me and be astonished; put your finger upon your mouth. Even I, whenever I remember it, am afraid, and trembling shakes my flesh.

Why, then, do the wicked live, and are lifted up and strengthened by riches? Their offspring remain before them; a multitude of relatives and descendants are in their sight. Their houses are secure and peaceful, and the rod of God is not upon them. Their ox conceives and does not miscarry; their cow gives birth and is not deprived of her young. Their little ones go out like flocks, and their children exult in their games; they hold the tambourine and lyre, and rejoice at the sound of the organ. They spend their days in prosperity, and in an instant descend to the underworld.

They say to God, ‘Depart from us; we do not want the knowledge of your ways. Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what benefit will it bring us if we pray to him?’ Nevertheless, because their good fortune is not in their own hand, let the counsel of the wicked be far from me.

How often will the lamp of the wicked be extinguished, and a flood come upon them, and he divide sorrows in his wrath? They will be like straw before the face of the wind, and like chaff that the whirlwind scatters. God will store up the pain of that man’s father for his children; and when he repays him, then he will know. His eyes will see their slaughter [Vulgate: his own slaughter], and he will drink from the wrath of the Almighty.

For what does he care about his house after him? And what if the number of his months is cut short? Can anyone teach God knowledge, who judges those on high? This man dies strong and healthy, rich and prosperous. His inward parts are full of fat, and his bones are moistened with marrow. But another dies in bitterness of soul, without any possessions; yet together they sleep in the dust, and worms cover them.

Certainly I know your thoughts and your unjust judgments against me. For you say, ‘Where is the house of the ruler? And where are the tents of the wicked?’ Ask any traveler, and you will learn that he understands these same things. For the wicked man is kept for the day of destruction, and he is led to the day of wrath. Who will confront him with his way? And who will repay him for what he has done? He himself will be led to the tomb, and he will keep watch over the heap of the dead. The gravel of Cocytus was sweet to him, and after him he will drag every human being, and before him innumerable others.

How, then, do you console me in vain, when your answer has been shown to contradict the truth?”

[Col. 1435D] Just as a perfect man is not moved by injuries, but calmly begs them to give ear to his words, so that, once they have heard and understood them, they may recognize themselves as deserving repentance. Wait patiently. If this should be fitting. If he were judging in this way among human beings, I would not be surprised, since among them what is just is sometimes unjustly judged. Marvel at how the one who is called just acts toward me in such a manner. This is a sign of silence. For although previously I thought that I was living rightly, I shudder at this, because I do not know what I am suffering, and I cannot approach the secret of the true God.

He answered those who say that the wicked should be swiftly destroyed [read: “swiftly”]. The succeeding generation. Kinship by blood. Not only sons, but also descendants in their sight. Their households, having no discord. A harsh correction. The offspring receives it.

[Col. 1436B] Before the proper time it does not give birth. She has given birth. She has not miscarried her calves. For the owners of flocks, the first blessing is that the flock, without barrenness, conceives. The second is that conception reaches birth; the third, that what has been born is brought to maturity through nourishment. He often shows that all these things are present among the wicked. And just as greater things have been granted for possession, so also many offspring may spring up for preservation.

When masters swell with honors and possessions, their dependents rejoice in childish entertainments. In temporal things. Like shadows. And within a very brief time they descend to the torments of hell, because every length of the present life is understood to be an instant when it is brought to an end.

He reveals the cause of the destruction of the wicked.

[Col. 1436C] Because their glory, which appeared temporal, will not endure. Because in place of this temporal glory they will put on perpetual disgrace. Temporal glory. Abundance of torments. He will repay each one. Sinners and the wicked will perish in such a way that they cannot be restored at all. When God repays, the Devil suffers eternal punishments with those who consent to him.

[Col. 1436D] Then the Devil will know—that is, he will feel it when he suffers. That is, the punishment, because there is a double misery: to suffer and to see. Others have said, “and he will not be saved by the Lord.” For he already knows that he will be condemned eternally together with his children, who are his household.

The Devil, when God divided the happiness that he had in heaven, and that immortal happiness was severed. Who can say to God, “Why do you do such things?”—the things mentioned above. He says that the condition of the blessed in this world and of the unhappy is common.

[Col. 1437A] Thus even now we see that some grow fat on abundance, while others waste away in extreme poverty. Just as the condition of the rich and the poor in being born is one, so also it is one in dying. Because in your thoughts you pronounce an unjust judgment against me. You mock and insult me. If you doubt whether these things are true, inquire of others, and they will tell you the same things I am saying.

Because here there is no separation between good and evil. Because God has appointed a day on which he will judge the world. The wicked man for the judgment of vengeance.

[Col. 1437B] The ancient enemy, or the wicked man in this world. Unless God intervenes. The wicked man for the death of torments, that is. For the increase of the Devil in sins. The wicked man is entangled while he watches the one whom he seduces. This is hell for the children of sin, whom the Devil deceives by the sweetness of sin. By imitation of his pride. He himself will follow those whom he deceived into punishment.

Here he brings his entire argumentative dispute to a conclusion, saying that his friends contend against him without cause, because they assert that he is tormented for impiety; whereas he, on the contrary, has proved that the wicked often prosper in this world.

## CHAPTER XXII

[Col. 1437C]

Eliphaz the Temanite responded and said:

“Can a human being be compared with God, even if he possesses perfect knowledge? What benefit is it if you are righteous? Or what do you contribute to him if your life is blameless? Will he reprove you because he fears you, and enter into judgment with you? Is it not rather because of your great wickedness and your endless iniquities?

For you took your brothers’ pledge without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing. You did not give water to the weary, and you withheld bread from the hungry. By the strength of your arm you possessed the land, and as the most powerful you held it. You sent widows away empty-handed, and crushed the arms of orphans [Vulgate: broke them]. Therefore you are surrounded by snares, and sudden fear troubles you. You thought you would not see darkness, and that you would not be overwhelmed by the force of overflowing waters.

Do you think that God is higher than heaven, and exalted above the heights of the stars? And you say, ‘What does God know? Does he judge as through a mist? The clouds are his hiding place; he does not consider our affairs, and he walks around the hinges of heaven.’

Do you wish to guard the ancient path, which wicked men have trodden? They were taken away before their time, and a river overturned their foundations. They said to God, ‘Depart from us’; and they regarded the Almighty as though he could do nothing, although he had filled their houses with good things. May their counsel be far from me.

The righteous will see and rejoice, and the innocent will mock them. Has not their pride been cut down, and has not fire devoured their remnant?

Acquiesce, then, and be at peace; in this way you will always have the best fruits. Receive the law from his mouth, and place his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; and you will remove iniquity far from your tent. He will give you flint in place of earth, and golden streams in place of flint. The Almighty will be against your enemies, and silver will be heaped up for you.

Then you will overflow with delights because of the Almighty, and you will lift your face toward God. You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows. You will decree a matter, and it will come to you, and light will shine upon your ways. For the one who has been humbled will be exalted in glory, and the one who has lowered his eyes will himself be saved. The innocent will indeed be saved; he will be saved by the purity of his hands.”

[Col. 1437C] However learned you may think yourself, you cannot be compared with God’s knowledge. No one makes God better by his righteousness; from him every source of righteousness proceeds. He says this with a mocking intent. If God, fearing you, were to contend with you in judgment, he explains below the causes of the individual iniquities.

In the manner of an enemy he seized another’s property, or unjustly extorted pledges. What does a plunderer deserve, if even one who refuses is condemned? Just as the Lord commands that drink be given to the thirsty.

[Col. 1437D] It is a serious matter to refuse bread, and more serious to take it away. He marks him as proud and tyrannical, because he rebuked his subjects not with fairness but with cruelty. Because he could not obtain from you what he requested. While you allowed them to be oppressed. As though he were saying: Troubled by fear of a guilty conscience, you have even lost the counsel of patience. You did not believe that you would receive the evil deserved by your deeds. The distress of calamities and miseries has burst upon you.

[Col. 1438A] He reproaches holy Job for not believing that God is everywhere: “Do you think that God is unaware of what you do?”—that he exists but is confined to the dwelling places of heaven and is inferior to the kingdom. By these words he asserts that holy Job says that God is deceived, or even errs in his judgments, doubting the true judgment. He accuses holy Job of falling into error by saying that the world is not governed by divine providence. As though, in holy Job’s own understanding, he were saying that God did not know him to be innocent and therefore allowed him to be wearied.

Do you wish to imitate the life of those who perished in the flood and in Sodom? Such as Dathan and Abiram, whom hell received when the earth split open. As wrath threatened them, the stability of their life was overturned.

[Col. 1438B] Therefore they were condemned for apostasy. Holy Job is not like that. For they thought that God would not pour vengeance upon sinners. As though he were saying: Why did they not fear God, lest his blessings be taken away from them? He placed holy Job among the blasphemers. For God’s justice is pleasing to them, just as they themselves are pleasing to God; and they will rejoice over themselves when they see others suffering.

Their pride, certainly, has been utterly destroyed. The uttermost consequences of sins, to be punished by tribulation on the day of judgment. He urges holy Job to turn back to God through repentance.

[Col. 1438C] After the blow, you will receive peace and recompense from God. Hear what he commands and preserve it. If you repent of your deeds, you will daily restore what is necessary. The Devil himself, who is the author of all iniquities, is indicated here. In place of soft things, strong ones; or in place of earthly things, heavenly ones. In place of a hardened heart, living waters of wisdom.

When you have obtained these things I have mentioned, the Almighty will be your defender. The word of the Lord is to be understood.

[Col. 1438D] You will be filled, enriched with spiritual delights. You will raise your brow freely in prayer to God. It is clear. A matter that is just, at least. In your good works, the light of the knowledge of God will shine for you. According to the Gospel: “Whoever humbles himself will be exalted” (Luke 14:11). The same meaning as in the preceding verse. Doing no evil. Through the grace of good works.

## CHAPTER XXIII

[Col. 1439A]

Job responded and said:

“Even now my speech is in bitterness, and the hand of my plague is heavier than my groaning. Who will grant me that I may know and find him, and come even to his throne? I will set my judgment before him, and fill my mouth with accusations. Let me know the words with which he will answer me, and understand what he will say to me.

I do not want him to contend with me through great fear, nor crush me by the weight of his greatness. Let him set fairness against me, and let my judgment reach victory. If I go to the east, he does not appear; if to the west, I do not understand him. If to the left, what shall I do? I shall not apprehend him; if I turn to the right, I shall not see him.

But he knows my way, and has tested me like gold that has passed through fire. My foot has followed his tracks; I have kept his way and have not turned aside from it. I have not withdrawn from the commands of his lips, and I have hidden the words of his mouth in my bosom. He is alone, and no one can turn aside his thoughts; whatever his soul has wished, that he has done.

When he has fulfilled his will concerning me, many other similar things are also ready for him. And therefore I am troubled before his face; considering him, I am anxious with fear. God has softened my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me. For I have not perished because of the darkness that threatens, nor has the gloom covered my face.”

[Col. 1439A] Having left behind the conversations of his friends, who add bitterness to my sorrow by their words, I will turn to God and say to him, relying on the confidence of my conscience, what follows.

He says that he knows God through understanding. Through good works. On the day of judgment, even to the contemplation of divine power. From him I shall seek the fairness of his judgment. That is, I shall speak with confidence. From the answer of my Lord I shall learn what cause there was for an innocent man to be assigned the torments of evils.

Throughout this entire little book, holy Job’s complaint to God has one meaning.

[Col. 1439B] His power, because no creature can endure it. He repeats the same thing. He speaks as one wishing, not commanding. That I may emerge victorious on the grounds of justice. While he enumerates all parts of the world, he says that God dwells everywhere in his entirety; yet he confesses that he is wholly invisible to him. He shows him to be invisible to creatures.

Because he knew his way of life very well. Just as gold is refined by fire, so he tests me through tribulations.

[Col. 1439C] I imitated his commands. And I kept what he wished to command; in the other part. As David says: “I have hidden your words in my heart” (Psalm 118:11). Because it is always his nature. That is, he cannot hide from God’s knowledge. Whatever he has decreed, he cannot pass over.

When he has afflicted me with torments as he wishes, he will still be able to inflict upon me as much more as he wishes. By the power of his majesty.

[Col. 1439D] Weighing it in thought. He unloosed me through terror, loosening my inward parts with fear. I have not yet been driven into despair because of the wounds I suffer. Unbelief has not covered my faith.

## CHAPTER XXIV

“Times are not hidden from the Almighty. But those who know him do not know his days. Others moved boundary markers, plundered flocks, and fed them. They drove away the donkey of orphans, and took the widow’s ox as a pledge. They overturned the way of the poor, and together oppressed the meek of the earth.

Others, like wild asses in the desert, go out to their work, watching for prey, and prepare bread for their children. They reap a field that is not theirs, and harvest the vineyard of the one whom they have oppressed by force. They leave people naked, taking away the garments of those who have no covering in the cold; those whom the rains of the mountains drench, and who, having no shelter, embrace the rocks.

They used violence, plundering orphans, and stripped the multitude of the poor. From the naked who went about without clothing, and from the hungry, they took the ears of grain. Among their heaps they rested at midday, while those who tread the winepresses thirst.

They made men groan from the cities, and the soul of the wounded cried out; yet God does not permit this to go unavenged. They were rebels against the light; they did not know its ways, nor did they return by its paths.

At first light the murderer rises; he kills the needy and the poor, but at night he becomes like a thief. The eye of the adulterer watches for darkness, saying, ‘No eye will see me’; and he covers his face so that he will not be recognized [Vulgate: he has no covering so that he will be recognized]. In the darkness they break into houses, as they had agreed with one another by day, and they do not know the light.

If dawn suddenly appears, they regard it as the shadow of death. Thus they walk in darkness as though in light. He is swift upon the face of the water; let his portion be cursed upon the earth, and let him not walk by the way of the vineyards. He has passed from the waters of snow to excessive heat; his sin reaches to the underworld.

Let mercy forget him; let worms be his sweetness. Let him not be remembered, but let him be crushed like a fruitless tree. For he fed the barren woman and the one who does not give birth, and he did not deal kindly with the widow.

He dragged down the strong by his strength; and when he stands, he will not trust his own life. God gave him a place for repentance, and he abuses it in pride. His eyes, however, are raised on his ways for a little while [Vulgate: are upon his ways]. They will not endure, but will be humbled [Vulgate: will be humbled like dreams and removed like, etc.], and will be taken away like dreams, and crushed like the tops of ears of grain.

And if this is not so, who can convict me of having lied and set my words before God?”

[Col. 1439D] Because he knows everything, since he created all things. Because no one knows him completely.

Against the command of Moses: “Do not move the boundaries that your fathers established.” They consumed the possessions of others.

From this point to the end, he spoke very obscurely, now in the plural, now in the singular.

[Col. 1440A] They act against the Law, where it says: “You shall not oppress the widow and the orphan by slander.” Stripping them of their possessions, or afflicting them through persecution. Those who could not resist, they subjected to slavery. Like bandits, they secretly seize what belongs to others. Certainly not for the work of God. With every vigilance they devote themselves to preparing food for themselves and their children from the possessions of others.

They steal the produce of fields. They plunder another’s vineyards. They do not fulfill the command: “If you see someone naked, cover him,” at the time when this was most useful.

[Col. 1440B] They are copiously drenched by waters flowing down from the mountains. Those who have no covering are sheltered beneath the shade of rocks. He marks them in two respects: in using force and in oppressing the orphan.

It is clear that they display strong vices against weak minds. They deceive them with flatteries. Having abandoned the fear and observance of God, they go beyond hostility and do not refrain from stripping even those who are half-naked. The very law of nature, or the fruit of good will.

This is a most wicked evil: that some rest beneath the fruits of others, because some become drunk on their wine.

[Col. 1440C] The devastation of the city reached the groaning of those who lived in the city. Of all the afflicted, whether those struck in the body by the sword or those wounded in spirit by the sorrow of fear. He does not allow the enemy to remain without vengeance.

Enemies, certainly, of God, who is the true light. The justice of the light mentioned above. They did not wish to return to God through repentance.

“Morning” is said because evil is committed publicly and in broad daylight. But it can also be understood of unjust judges, who rise early for the purpose of subverting the case of the needy and poor, having been corrupted by gifts. He ought to have shown them mercy.

The public murderer also becomes a nocturnal thief. The eye of his heart flees from knowledge of the light of God, because he did not wish to understand in order to act well.

[Col. 1440D] He meditates on breaking into houses in darkness. By day they determined among themselves adulterous conversations. That is, concerning Christ. If the light of life is brought upon them through God’s chastisement, because of the evil of their conscience they think that they are suffering death.

They take such delight in living in sins as they ought to have lived in the light of virtues.

He speaks of sinners who possess no weight of good works. He called that portion cursed which belongs not to God but to the world.

[Col. 1441A] So that he does not follow the faith of the Church. The wicked now feel burning fire, now excessive cold. Vengeance in the underworld. God, who is called not only merciful but also Mercy. Sins belong to sinners. May he not pertain to the mercy that grants pardon. The Devil, who never bears the fruit of repentance.

He nourished sin in the human being; or, souls without the fruits of virtues. Good works from the heart. He calls him a human soul that does not possess God and is deprived of the powers of holiness, whom he did not wish to admonish to return.

If he overthrew the strong, consider what he did to the weak. He does not believe that he can remain standing in his ruined life.

[Col. 1441B] So that he cannot excuse himself. He despised the benefit of mercy through pride. Now they are spoken of in the plural, although earlier he had spoken of them in the singular. They will soon fail. Because the present life is brief, the useless condition of the wicked is compared with sleep. The Devil and the wicked man are crushed with such ease that they are reduced to nothing.

If you do not think it is as I have said, who among you can convict me of falsehood? You who say that in this present time God adds to sinners everything they deserve, and assert this to my disgrace.

## CHAPTER XXV

Baldad the Shuhite responded and said:

“Power and terror belong to him who makes peace in his high places. Is there any number to his armies? And upon whom does his light not shine [Vulgate: will his light rise]? Can a human being be justified when compared with God, or can one born of a woman appear clean?

Behold, even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not clean in his sight. How much less a human being, who is rottenness, and a son of man, who is a worm!”

[Col. 1441C] Baldad, having been refuted, said: He does not now execute judgment, but postpones it for the future and keeps it stored up with himself. Yet he will possess peace jointly among his holy ones, or among his angels. The number of his armies is infinite. For he himself illuminates every human being who comes into this world.

Baldad is not responding to what holy Job said, but, following the same line of thought, he says what they had often said.

[Col. 1441D] Angels and the heavenly powers cannot be compared with God. Since a worm is born from corruption, so also is a human being.

## CHAPTER XXVI

Job responded and said:

“Whose helper are you? Is it of the weak? Do you sustain the arm of one who is not strong? To whom have you given counsel? Perhaps to one who lacks wisdom? And you have displayed your abundant prudence.

Whom did you wish to teach? Was it not the one who made your breath? Behold, the giants groan beneath the waters, and those who dwell with them. Hell is naked before him, and destruction has no covering.

He stretches out the north over emptiness, and hangs the earth upon nothing. He binds up the waters in his clouds, so that they do not burst forth together below. He holds back the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud over it. He has drawn a boundary around the waters, until light and darkness come to an end.

The pillars of heaven tremble and fear his arrival. By his strength the seas suddenly gather together, and by his wisdom he strikes down pride. His Spirit adorned the heavens, and by his hand, which brings forth, the twisting serpent was brought out.

Behold, these things have been spoken in part concerning his ways; and when we have scarcely heard a small drop of his words, who can behold the thunder of his greatness?”

[Col. 1441D] Holy Job never answered his friends harshly when they inflicted open injuries upon him. But now, seeing an injury done to God, he was moved by righteous indignation and reproved Baldad in words, because he spoke as though God were weak and needed assistance.

Blessed Job marvels at how he dared to teach the one from whom he himself exists.

[Col. 1442A] That is, your soul. The Devil, or proud human beings. Beneath the earth, that is, in hell. All unbelievers together. Nothing can be hidden from the knowledge of God. The Devil cannot conceal himself from the power of God’s majesty.

He calls it the north because it is impenetrable and remote in profound silence. Because it was made from nothing, or because it is supported by no support. They are now said to be bound because they are not poured out all at once upon the earth, as we read happened in the Flood.

[Col. 1442B] The decree and terror of his judgment. His concealment, because few know the secrets of God. God will not allow his holy ones to be afflicted beyond measure by unbelieving peoples. Because at the end of the world these things cease to vary in this way.

Angels are so called for adornment. They venerate the presence of their Creator. Here blessed Job recounts God’s power to Baldad, so that he would not imagine himself God’s helper.

The Devil, who was cast down from the lofty seat of heaven. The Holy Spirit, the Apostles. When teachers bring forth children of faith, the Lord assists them by his piety, so that they may produce such offspring. The crafty beast harms his holy ones, from whom he is excluded, so that he may no longer have power over them.

[Col. 1442C] In him there is nothing crooked. He says above that no one can comprehend everything. He calls the assumed human being the stone said in Daniel to have been cut out. For this is what he says: If we do not fully understand the assumed human being, who in comparison with the God who assumes him is a very small drop, how much less can we understand the divinity itself? Because divinity is compared with thunder, which thundered from heaven over the earth.

## CHAPTER XXVII

Job also continued, taking up his parable, and said:

“As God lives, who has taken away my judgment, and the Almighty, who has brought bitterness upon my soul: as long as breath remains in me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils, my lips will not speak iniquity, nor will my tongue meditate deceit.

Far be it from me to judge you righteous. Until I perish, I will not depart from my innocence. I will not abandon my justification, which I have begun to hold; for my heart does not reproach me throughout all my life.

Let my enemy be regarded as the wicked man, and my adversary as the unjust. For what hope does the hypocrite have if he greedily snatches away, and God does not deliver his soul? Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him? Or can he delight in the Almighty and invoke God at every time?

I will teach you by the hand of God; I will not conceal what the Almighty possesses. Behold, you all know it; why do you speak vainly without cause?

This is the portion of the wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the violent, which they will receive from the Almighty. If his children are multiplied, they will be for the sword, and his descendants will not be satisfied with bread. Those who remain of him will be buried in destruction, and his widows will not weep.

If he heaps up silver like dust and prepares garments like clay, he will indeed prepare them, but the righteous will clothe himself with them, and the innocent will divide the silver.

He built his house like a moth, and made a shelter like a watchman. When the rich man sleeps, he will take nothing away with him; he will open his eyes, and find nothing.

Poverty will seize him like water; a storm will overwhelm him by night. A scorching wind will carry him away, and a whirlwind will take him away. It will snatch him from his place and hurl itself upon him, and it will not spare him. Fleeing from his hand, he will flee; it will tighten its hands over him and hiss at him while looking upon his place.”

[Col. 1442C] He indicates that what he had previously said he would say chiefly by way of a parable. By this oath—later, where the Prophets are. While he permits him to suffer, he takes away. He says that he does what he wishes under judgment. He is heard; he lives.

[Col. 1442D] He says that what belongs to the administration of a just judgment has been taken away for a time. He speaks of the present misery with which he is filled. My breath is already weakened. He who strengthens me so that I may endure these torments. So that I may call you righteous. Which you assert I have lost, as though through my blasphemies.

Until I live, I will not abandon my justification. Here “all life” is to be understood as his present life, during the time when he was saying these things, because he did not consent to those giving evil advice and urging the blasphemy of the one who prophesied.

He seems to say this more by the Spirit than as a wish to curse. He who is also separated from me in faith, who does not agree with me in conduct. That is, false and deceitful in friendship. As though you were suffering from a thirst for greed for my destruction, if you do not obey God and take care to correct yourselves in this life.

For then the wicked will begin to cry out to God, when there will be no opportunity for them to be heard. When vengeance comes upon the wicked, there will be no remedy. The one who has presented himself in such a way that he deserves to be heard at any time can delight in God and invoke him.

He says those things that God has in his power, which he also wishes to demonstrate to them.

[Col. 1443B] Because you bring forth all these things against me personally. Things without reason. As though he were saying: The wicked and violent will receive the things that follow not only now but also in the future judgment from God Almighty.

In sons and descendants he saw the entire posterity of an evil generation. Because they are alienated from knowledge of the truth. Imitators of evil parents are condemned to future death. Certainly, they will not have sufficient time.

The greatness of the greed of the wicked is compared with the materials of earth and clay because of the immensity of their riches.

[Col. 1443C] Taking away, and granting to believers the eloquence for preaching the Gospel, through which souls are clothed. As Solomon says: “The riches of sinners are stored up for the righteous”; or Christ, the eloquence of worldly people.

Thus he rests in his prosperity. His joy passed so quickly. When he enters the sleep of death, he will possess nothing of his wealth. At the resurrection he will find no merit of good work.

The previously mentioned rich man is overtaken by sudden poverty. In his blindness. Tribulation. The sentence of God condemning him.

[Col. 1443D] Suddenly, it will not come upon him with violence. From the body. God will impose the deserved punishment upon him, repaying him according to his deeds. He will not be held by the hand so as to be saved. Others have said: “He will clap his hands over him and drag him from his place.” It signifies the fierceness of the punishment.

## CHAPTER XXVIII

“Silver has the beginnings of its veins, and gold has a place where it is smelted. [Col. 1444A] Iron is taken from the earth, and stone, loosened by heat, is turned into bronze.

He has set a limit for darkness, and he himself considers the end of all things, even the stone of gloom and the shadow of death. A torrent divides from the people who wander; those whom the foot of the needy has forgotten, and those without a path.

The earth from which bread arose is overturned by fire in [Col. 1444B] its place. Its stones are the place of sapphires, and its clods are gold. The bird does not know the path, nor has the vulture’s eye looked upon it. The sons of merchants have not trodden it, nor has the lioness passed through it.

He stretches out his hand to the flint; he overturns mountains from their roots. In the rocks he cuts channels, and his eye sees every [Col. 1444C] precious thing. He also searches out the depths of rivers and brings hidden things into the light.

But where is wisdom found, and what is the place of understanding? A human being does not know its price, nor is it found in the land of those who live in ease. The abyss says, ‘It is not in me’; and the sea says, ‘It is not [Col. 1444D] with me.’

Refined gold will not be given for it, nor will silver be weighed in exchange for it. It will not be compared with the dyed colors of India, nor with the most precious sardonyx stone or sapphire. Gold and glass will not equal it; vessels of gold will not be counted in exchange for it. Lofty and eminent things will not be mentioned in comparison with it.

Wisdom, however, is drawn from hidden [Col. 1445A] places. Ethiopian topaz will not equal it, nor will the purest dye be combined with it.

From where, then, will wisdom come, and what is the place of understanding? It is hidden from the eyes of all living things; it is concealed even from the birds of heaven.

Destruction and death said, ‘With our ears we have heard its report.’ God understands its way; he himself knows its place. For he looks upon the ends of the world and sees all [Col. 1445B] things beneath heaven.

He established weight for the winds and measured the waters. When he appointed a law for the rains and a way for the resounding storms, then he saw it, declared it, prepared it, and searched it out.

And he said to the human being: ‘Behold, the fear of God is itself wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding.’”

[Col. 1443D] The holy man’s eloquence of faith, arising from the perceptions of the soul, is directed toward spiritual understanding. For in tribulation he is tested like gold in the fire.

[Col. 1444A] Strength is perfected from weakness. Hard of heart, through the fervor of faith, into a resonant confession. An end to sins, or to sinful people. What reward a person is to receive. The devil on account of his errors. That his teaching is followed by death. The passion of Christ separates the wicked from the saints, who are pilgrims here. Christ has forgotten those who did not believe the Gospel. In the foot also observe Christ’s dispensation, by which he separates from the saints those living without the path of religion. He who became poor for our sake. It is as though he is now speaking of Sodom, which was exceedingly fertile and was overthrown by fire because of the sins of its inhabitants. It is as though these kinds of gems are mentioned in place of the wealth of the Sodomites.

[Col. 1444B] Because through these things it is usually acquired. Frightened away from the estates, because, owing to the great number of people, scarcely any birds could be there. It was covered by such dense shade of trees that birds flying above could not see it. Because the earth itself produced almost everything for it. Of merchants, who, because of their eagerness for profit, were also called the sons of merchants in their descendants. Because of the multitude of peoples, wild beasts could not pass through there. Now he turns to Christ, to the strength of his virtue. The proud—or, finally, the devil—overthrown. At the coming of the Son of God. In the Apostles, or among the Gentiles, those who had previously been hard. He gave his grace. As it says:

[Col. 1444C] “The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous.” The hidden matters of the consciences of people who hasten toward death as though they were rivers: their wickedness. Into revelation. He says that it cannot be found by a human being unless God reveals it. It becomes so precious that a person utterly fails to know how great its worth is; no price, however, is worthy of it. Among those who serve the pleasures of the flesh in a worldly manner. Hell is signified. Because worldly people do not possess the wisdom of the love of God. This does not signify the present world. He says that no thing, however precious it may be, can be compared with this wisdom.

[Col. 1444D] He indicates here that no one can perceive or express this wisdom according to its worth. By India all worshipers of idols are signified, for there precious worshipers are born. Who are precious stones. That the religion of idols falsely shines with the name of divinity. Famous people are understood, who in this world shine by the name of dignity and by the glory of riches. For the nobles of this world are reckoned as nothing if they do not possess the fear of God. The heights of this world will be unworthy of remembrance in comparison with that wisdom. By the gift of the Holy Spirit. It is taken from things above.

[Col. 1445A] He brought all these names to remembrance because no creature can be compared with the fear of God. He says this in the same sense as above: “Where is wisdom found?”—that is, among all who live carnally in the world. Proud or frivolous people, who think lofty thoughts while dwelling in low things, are understood. The devil and his attendants. They perceived it, but through disobedience they did not wish to possess it. God certainly knows where wisdom is hastening, and he himself also provides it with guidance, namely, to the place of eternal peace. Visiting us in the fullness of time.

[Col. 1445B] As it says in the Psalm: “The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men” (Ps. XIII, 2). The grace of the Holy Spirit, or even of the angels themselves. He calls these “teachings,” because he says that, through the effect of divine sanctification, they possess weight. He wished to indicate the teaching of both Testaments. Through the persecutions of the Church he opens a way for passing onward, so that they may not overcome his saints. He foresaw the future fear of God in the world. Through the mouth of the prophets, seeking the wandering sheep. Now he explains what he had said above in a more obscure manner.

## CHAPTER XXIX

[Col. 1445B] That holy Job is about to speak what follows in the form of a parable is recognized from the inscription of the title itself.

[Col. 1445C] Job also continued, taking up his parable, and said:

“Who will grant me that I might be as in the months of former days, and according to the days when God guarded me? When his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through darkness? As I was in the days of my youth, when God was secretly in my tent? When the Almighty was with me, and my children all around me? When I washed my feet with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me? When I went out to the gate of the city, and they prepared a chair for me in the marketplace? Young men saw me and hid themselves, and old men, rising, stood. Princes ceased speaking and placed a finger upon their mouths. Leaders restrained their voices, and their tongue clung to their throat. The ear that heard blessed me,

[Col. 1446A] and the eye that saw bore witness to me, because I had delivered the poor man who cried out, and the orphan who had no helper. The blessing of the child [Vulgate: ‘of the perishing child’] came upon me, and I consoled the widow’s heart. I put on righteousness, and I clothed myself, as with a garment and a diadem, with my judgment. I was an eye to the blind and a foot to the lame. I was a father to the poor.

[Col. 1446B] And the case that I did not know I investigated with the greatest care. I crushed the jaws of the wicked, and snatched the prey from his teeth. And I said: ‘In my little nest I shall die, and like the palm tree I shall multiply my days.’ My root was spread out beside the waters, and dew would remain upon my harvest. My glory would always be renewed, and my bow would be restored in my hand.

[Col. 1446C] Those who heard me waited for my decision [absent in the Vulgate], and attentive, they were silent at my counsel. They did not dare to add anything to my words, and my eloquence dripped upon them. They waited for me like rain, and opened their mouths as though for the late rain. If ever I laughed at them, they did not believe it, and the light of my face

[Col. 1446D] did not fall to the ground. If I had wished to go to them, I sat first; and when I sat like a king with an army surrounding him, I was nevertheless a comforter of the sorrowful.”

[Col. 1445B] He desires to be recalled to that happiness which he had once possessed together with God’s protection. To his former happiness. In which he lived prosperously. Temporal glory. Clearly above the rest. Among sinners, certainly, and I walked toward those things that I did not know, prospering through his virtue. The Almighty dwelt spiritually in my heart, once the tumult of vices had been removed. When I enjoyed God’s presence. The virtues of the soul stood beside him.

[Col. 1445D] He washed the steps of his soul with the simplicity of good works. The Son of the Most High gave generously. The Holy Spirit’s abundant blessings. Because judges sat at the gate in order to judge those entering the city. When the time came for examining different cases, they prepared a chair for me in the marketplace, as for a teacher. In these verses he displays the reverent fear that old and young men, princes and judges, rightly showed toward him. His conduct was so holy,

[Col. 1446A] and his reputation reported it, that everyone praised him. I delivered from the hand of the violent man the oppressed needy person who indicated by his cry that he was suffering violence. I rescued from the wicked the orphan deprived of the aid of a defender. In widows, orphans, and children he designates every kind of humble and afflicted person—or, as others have said, the poor—none of whom he despised. As it says: “Let your priests be clothed with righteousness” (Ps. CXXXI, 9). Mercy and truth were the garments of his soul. A royal crown, because in him the truth of judgment stood out like a diadem. In these words he displays the affection of his compassion. I showed them a father’s affection.

[Col. 1446B] So that they would not be oppressed by any device of their adversaries. The stronger are designated by the jaws for devouring. He calls him a rapacious man, from whose mouth he violently removed the poor man’s substance. In the flesh, because the wise person dies daily before himself through fear of the day of judgment. He desires his days to be blessed in the resurrection. My hope and faith, which are directed toward this expectation of mine, are open to the divine words. The remembrance of the divine word in the time of tribulation. The fruit of the believer continually increases for eternal joy. A strong resistance against vices is signified.

[Col. 1446C] He indicates the astonishment of his hearers and how they revered him. He says this on account of his wisdom, because among them not only was his wisdom exalted, but his counsel was also exceedingly useful. His authority was so great that no one dared to say anything except what he said. His teaching penetrated their understanding. By the names of rain and shower he demonstrates that his knowledge was exceedingly abundant. He says this on account of the gravity of his conduct. They marveled when they saw me laughing. The customary serenity of his face was disturbed in vain. And therefore, whatever they observed in the serenity of his face,

[Col. 1446D] they received as something great and exceptional. By going to those beneath him, he showed his humility. In the power of kingship he offered consolation to the wretched and sorrowful.

## CHAPTER XXX

“Now, however, the younger men in age mock me, whose fathers I would not deem worthy to be placed among the dogs of my flock. Their strength of hands was of no account to me, and they themselves were considered

[Col. 1447A] unworthy of life. Barren through poverty and hunger, they gnawed in the wilderness. Squalid with calamity and misery, they ate grasses [Vulgate: ‘chewed’] and the bark of trees, and the root of junipers was their food. Those who, snatching these things from the valleys, whenever they found anything at all, ran toward it with a cry. They lived in the deserts, in the ravines, and in caves of the earth, or upon gravel. They rejoiced among such things and considered it a delight to be beneath thorn bushes. Sons of fools and men without renown,

[Col. 1447B] and utterly absent from the earth. Now I have become their song, and I have become their proverb. They abhor me, flee far from me, and are not afraid to spit in my face. For he opened his quiver and afflicted me, placed a bridle in my mouth, and at the right hand of the rising one of my calamity they immediately rose up. They overturned my feet and oppressed me as though with the waves of their paths. They destroyed my roads,

[Col. 1447C] they lay in wait for me, prevailed, and there was no one to bring help. As though a wall had been broken and a gate opened, they rushed upon me and rolled down upon my miseries. I have been reduced to nothing, and you have taken away my desire like the wind; and like a cloud my salvation has passed away. Now my soul withers within me [Vulgate: ‘decays’], and days of affliction possess me. By night pain pierces

[Col. 1447D] my bones, and those who devour me do not sleep. In their multitude my garment is consumed, and like the collar of a tunic they have girded me [Vulgate: ‘they have girded me with the collar of a tunic’]. I have been compared with mud and made like dust and ashes. I cry to you, and you do not hear me; I stand, and you do not regard me. You have changed toward me into a cruel one,

[Col. 1448A] and in the harshness of your hand you oppose me. You have lifted me up and, setting me as though upon the wind, you have struck me down violently. I know that you will hand me over to death, where a house has been appointed for every living thing. Nevertheless, you will not send your hand for their destruction [Vulgate: ‘you send my hand for destruction’], and if they fall, you yourself will save them. Formerly I wept over the afflicted, and my soul had compassion
